The story does not establish the decision’s exact date.

USA.title: Warren calls Powell dangerous and opposes his reappointment
USA.summary: US Senator Elizabeth Warren called Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell a “dangerous man” and announced that she would oppose his reappointment, citing his easing of post-financial-crisis bank regulations. Her opposition came as President Biden considered whether to renominate Powell, whose term was due to end in February.

USA.title: Warren calls for SEC investigation of Fed officials' trading
USA.summary: US Senator Elizabeth Warren called on the Securities and Exchange Commission to investigate whether top Federal Reserve officials’ financial trades violated insider trading rules. Her request sought scrutiny of past transactions, including Richard Clarida’s portfolio trades shortly before Chair Jay Powell signaled pandemic support measures, rather than only prospective ethics reforms. The Fed said Clarida’s transactions were a preplanned portfolio rebalancing with prior approval.

USA.title: Warren questions Powell's leadership
USA.summary: Senator Elizabeth Warren criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on the Senate floor for what she called bad judgment in failing to prevent unusual trading by senior Fed officials. In a subsequent Bloomberg interview, she opposed his reappointment and called for someone else to replace him when his term ended. The reports placed her criticism before President Biden publicly expressed support for Powell.

USA.title: Biden voices confidence in Powell
USA.summary: President Joe Biden publicly expressed confidence in Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell following Senator Elizabeth Warren's criticism of his leadership. The support came as Powell's term approached renewal in February and senior Fed officials' stock trading faced scrutiny. Biden's remarks contained no reported monetary-policy demand or threat.

USA.title: Warren opposes Powell reappointment in Bloomberg interview
USA.summary: In a Bloomberg interview following her Senate floor criticism, US Senator Elizabeth Warren reiterated her opposition to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s renomination. She urged that he finish his term and be replaced, arguing that different leadership would leave the Fed better off and the economy safer.

USA.title: Biden order calls for scrutiny of bank merger competition
USA.summary: The Biden administration signed an executive order calling on the Federal Reserve to study the competitive effects of bank mergers and acquisitions. In an October 13, 2021 interview, fund manager Filippo Maria Alloatti cited the order as evidence of the administration's increased focus on banking competition. The story did not establish the order's exact signing date or report threats to Fed officials or institutional autonomy.

USA.title: Warren calls Powell dangerous at Senate hearing
USA.summary: At a Senate hearing in late September 2021, Senator Elizabeth Warren called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell a "dangerous man" to lead the central bank, criticizing his steps to ease bank regulations and opposing his appointment to a second term. The linked report does not establish the hearing's exact date.

USA.title: White House officials dismiss trading concerns over Powell's renomination
USA.summary: People familiar told Bloomberg that top White House officials saw no reason for concern over Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s October 2020 sale of $1 million to $5 million in an index fund and did not consider it disqualifying for renomination. The transaction occurred outside the Fed’s blackout period. Their position supported Powell’s prospects for a second term without advocating a monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Yellen endorses Powell for a second term
USA.summary: Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen, a former Federal Reserve chair, endorsed Jerome Powell for a second term as Fed chair while President Biden considered his choice. The endorsement supported Powell's reappointment without advocating a monetary policy direction.

USA.title: Elizabeth Warren opposes Powell's second term
USA.summary: Senator Elizabeth Warren said she would vote against a second term for Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. Reporting attributed her and other progressive Democrats’ opposition to their view that Powell had overseen looser bank regulations and had been too slow to make climate change a Fed priority. Despite this opposition, Powell was reported likely to win Senate confirmation following President Biden’s nomination announcement.

USA.title: Jeff Merkley opposes Powell's second term
USA.summary: Senator Jeff Merkley of Oregon said he would vote against a second term for Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. A November 22 report attributed progressive opposition to Powell’s oversight of looser bank regulations and perceived failure to make climate change a sufficient Fed priority. The report nevertheless said Powell had bipartisan support and was likely to be confirmed.

USA.title: Warren calls Powell a dangerous man over bank regulation
USA.summary: US Senator Elizabeth Warren called Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell a “dangerous man,” criticizing his insufficiently tough approach to banks and banking regulation. Coverage recalling her criticism reported that President Joe Biden nevertheless renominated Powell, with his economic crisis management and perceived steadiness outweighing regulatory criticism.

USA.title: Warren demands transparency over Fed trading scandal
USA.summary: U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren called for more information and greater transparency concerning the Federal Reserve trading scandal in remarks on Monday. Bloomberg reported her demands amid discussion of Richard Clarida’s early departure and scrutiny surrounding Jerome Powell’s confirmation hearing. No monetary-policy demand or threat was reported in her intervention.

USA.title: Biden nominates Raskin as Fed banking regulator
USA.summary: President Biden nominated former Federal Reserve governor Sarah Bloom Raskin as the Fed’s next top banking regulator. The report presented the nomination as signaling the administration’s desire for greater attention to climate-related financial risks. It did not establish a demand for broader monetary easing or tightening, or a proposed change to the Fed’s statutory mandate or autonomy.

USA.title: Lawmakers criticize Fed leadership at Senate hearing
USA.summary: Unnamed lawmakers criticized Federal Reserve leadership during Jerome Powell’s Senate testimony the day after Eric Rosengren and Robert Kaplan announced their early retirements in late September 2021. They described the officials’ trading controversy as a blow to the Fed’s impartiality and independence. Separate quoted criticisms called Powell dangerous for making the banking system less safe and said the Fed should serve the public rather than officials’ stock portfolios. The story does not establish that the trades violated ethics rules or identify an exact hearing date.

USA.title: Warren calls for SEC investigation of Fed officials
USA.summary: Senator Elizabeth Warren alleged a culture of corruption at the Federal Reserve and called for an SEC investigation following scrutiny of Vice Chair Richard Clarida’s February 27, 2020 transactions. Her statement also raised questions about regional Fed presidents Robert Kaplan and Eric Rosengren. Clarida said his trades were planned portfolio rebalancing; the story did not establish misconduct or date Warren’s statement precisely.

USA.title: Biden calls on Fed to address inflation
USA.summary: President Joe Biden called on the Federal Reserve to act against inflation, according to Julius Baer chief investment officer Yves Bonzon in a January 21 television interview referring to Biden's remarks a couple of days earlier. The reported demand urged inflation restraint but included no criticism of Fed competence or threats to its leadership or autonomy.

USA.title: Senate Republicans challenge Fed nominee on energy lending
USA.summary: At Sarah Bloom Raskin’s confirmation hearing for the Federal Reserve’s top banking regulator position, Senate Banking Committee Republicans challenged her previous calls for more aggressive regulation away from high-emissions investments. Raskin told senators she would not use the position to restrict lending to the oil and gas industry.

USA.title: Raskin urges Fed to prioritize inflation
USA.summary: At her Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing, Sarah Bloom Raskin, President Biden’s nominee to be the Federal Reserve’s top banking regulator, urged the Fed to prioritize tackling high inflation. Fellow Fed board nominees Lisa Cook and Philip Jefferson expressed the same priority. The report noted that the Fed had signaled interest-rate increases beginning in mid-March.

USA.title: Biden nominates three governors to broaden Fed perspectives
USA.summary: President Biden announced the nominations of Sarah Bloom Raskin, Philip Jefferson and Lisa Cook to three Federal Reserve Board vacancies, saying they would bring a diversity of thought and perspective never before seen on the board. The reporting presented his choices as aligned with his push for a more equal economy. Raskin was nominated for the bank-supervision role, while Cook would become the board’s first Black woman if confirmed. The announcement was dated only to January 2022.

USA.title: Kennedy challenges Raskin over fossil-fuel lending proposal
USA.summary: At Sarah Bloom Raskin’s Federal Reserve confirmation hearing, Senator John Kennedy repeatedly challenged her May 2020 proposal to exclude oil and gas companies from pandemic emergency lending. He characterized it as saving everyone except that industry and letting its companies fail. Raskin responded that her argument concerned a specific pandemic program and that the Fed should not pick winners and losers; Kennedy rejected that explanation. The February 8 report places the hearing in the previous week without establishing an exact date.

USA.title: Toomey rejects Raskin's assurances on Fed sector neutrality
USA.summary: In closing remarks at Sarah Bloom Raskin’s Federal Reserve confirmation hearing, Senator Pat Toomey dismissed her assurances that the Fed should not pick winners and losers as a “scripted mantra.” He argued that her speeches and other interventions had advocated precisely such selective treatment, challenging her stated commitment to sector neutrality. The February 8 report places the hearing in the preceding week but does not establish its exact date.

USA.title: Manchin urges Fed to confront inflation
USA.summary: Democratic Senator Joe Manchin urged the Federal Reserve to confront inflation and tackle rising prices head on in comments over the weekend before February 14, 2022. His intervention pressed the Fed toward tighter policy but included no reported threat or specific rate demand. The report did not establish the exact day of his comments.

USA.title: Manchin urges Fed to tackle inflation head on
USA.summary: U.S. Senator Manchin urged the Federal Reserve to tackle inflation head on, advocating stronger action against price pressures. The report provided no specific policy proposal or threat.

USA.title: Senate Republicans boycott vote on Fed nominees over Raskin
USA.summary: Senate Banking Committee Republicans boycotted a vote on President Biden’s five Federal Reserve nominees, delaying all five, including Chair Jerome Powell, over Sarah Bloom Raskin’s nomination as vice chair for supervision. They questioned whether she used government contacts to help payments firm Reserve Trust while serving on its board and said her answers were inadequate. Raskin said she complied with all ethical requirements. Republicans also cited her climate-policy comments, and Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell urged Biden to choose a different, more mainstream nominee.

USA.title: McConnell calls for replacement of Raskin nomination
USA.summary: Senate Minority Leader Mitch McConnell urged President Biden to find a better, more mainstream nominee to replace Sarah Bloom Raskin as his choice for Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision. His demand came amid Republicans blocking a vote on Biden's Fed nominees over questions they said Raskin had inadequately answered about her role on a fintech company's board.

USA.title: Biden pledges support for Fed inflation fight in WSJ opinion piece
USA.summary: In a Wall Street Journal opinion piece ahead of his meeting with Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, President Joe Biden pledged support for the Fed's efforts to combat high inflation while saying he would not influence its decisions. He emphasized the Fed's independence and contrasted his approach with Donald Trump's. The article outlined a three-part inflation strategy but specified no monetary policy demand or threat.

USA.title: Biden stresses Fed responsibility and independence at Powell meeting
USA.summary: At his third meeting with Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell since taking office, President Joe Biden emphasized the Fed's responsibility for fighting inflation while pledging respect for its independence. Council of Economic Advisers Chair Cecilia Rouse described his message as a commitment that the White House would stay out of the Fed's way. No specific policy change or threat was reported.

USA.title: Biden urges Powell to do what it takes against inflation
USA.summary: President Joe Biden told Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell in a meeting to do what it takes to fight inflation, while affirming the Fed's independence and pledging not to interfere. The June 8 report characterized Biden as supporting forceful inflation fighting despite higher interest rates, an economic slowdown and potential electoral costs; it did not specify the meeting date.

USA.title: Warren warns Fed against driving economy off a cliff
USA.summary: US lawmaker Elizabeth Warren urged the Federal Reserve to exercise caution in its inflation-fighting tightening, warning against driving the economy off a cliff. Her comments were cited in press reports discussed ahead of Chair Jerome Powell’s House Financial Services testimony, amid concerns about the economic costs of further tightening.

USA.title: Pat Toomey criticizes Fed's approach to inflation
USA.summary: In a broadcast clip, Pennsylvania Senator Pat Toomey criticized the Federal Reserve’s monetary-policy management, arguing that it treated inflation as a psychological rather than monetary problem. He prioritized bringing inflation under control quickly, warning of enormous long-term damage, while acknowledging a significant risk of recession within 12 months.

USA.title: Congressional report faults Fed response to Chinese espionage
USA.summary: A Republican-led congressional investigation alleged that China tried to recruit informants within the Federal Reserve and criticized the Fed's response as inadequate. The report did not establish whether sensitive information was compromised. Fed Chair Jerome Powell strongly disputed its findings and called its characterizations of some employees unfair. China denied conducting espionage.

USA.title: Congressional bill proposes audits for Fed rule deviations
USA.summary: A congressional bill proposed requiring the Federal Reserve to undergo an audit explaining deviations from a monetary policy rule, seeking to encourage rule-based policymaking. Then-Fed Chair Janet Yellen opposed such legislation as infringing Fed independence. The bill did not pass; the linked account places it in historical legislative efforts without establishing an exact date.

USA.title: Congress adds maximum employment to the Fed's mandate
USA.summary: In a historical account, Atlanta Fed President Raphael Bostic described Congress's passage of the Humphrey-Hawkins Act as adding maximum employment to the Federal Reserve's mandate alongside price stability. He said the change followed advocacy beginning in the late 1960s and early 1970s by activists, including Civil Rights Movement participants, for broader central-bank objectives. The account does not establish an exact date for the congressional action.

USA.title: Nixon urges lower rates at Burns's swearing-in
USA.summary: At Arthur Burns's 1970 swearing-in as Federal Reserve chairman, President Richard Nixon jokingly called the standing welcome advance appreciation for lower interest rates and more money. While professing respect for Burns's independence, Nixon said he hoped Burns would independently conclude that the president's views should be followed. The linked retrospective does not establish the ceremony's exact date.

USA.title: Warren challenges Powell over unemployment cost of tightening
USA.summary: At a Senate hearing, Senator Elizabeth Warren challenged Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the employment costs of monetary tightening, asking him to explain himself to two million workers she said he was planning to get fired over the next year. Her criticism opposed tightening that would increase unemployment. Powell responded that high inflation was hurting working people and questioned whether they would be better off if the Fed abandoned its efforts to control it.

USA.title: Senate Republicans urge Powell to continue fighting inflation
USA.summary: During Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's Senate Banking Committee appearance, Republican senators urged him to continue fighting inflation while blaming President Joe Biden for overstimulating the economy. Their demand supported continued monetary tightening as Powell indicated that interest rates might need to rise faster and reach a higher peak than previously expected.

USA.title: Sherrod Brown pushes Fed for stronger bank safeguards
USA.summary: In an interview about preventing another Silicon Valley Bank failure, Senate committee chair Sherrod Brown said he was pressing the Federal Reserve for stronger bank capital and liquidity standards and stress tests. He also pledged to push Congress for stronger safeguards, but expressed doubt it would act because of banking lobby and Wall Street influence.

USA.title: Patrick McHenry pledges congressional scrutiny of Fed supervision
USA.summary: In a Bloomberg interview, House Financial Services Committee Chairman Patrick McHenry pledged that Congress and his committee would investigate Silicon Valley Bank's collapse, including whether Federal Reserve supervision failed in Washington or San Francisco. Asked about the Fed investigating itself, he reaffirmed congressional scrutiny but cautioned against assigning blame before establishing the facts.

USA.title: Warren presses regulators to strengthen banking rules
USA.summary: During questioning of financial regulators, Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren pressed Federal Reserve Vice Chair for Supervision Michael Barr, FDIC Chair Martin Gruenberg and Treasury Under Secretary Nellie Liang to endorse stronger banking rules. She emphasized that preventing bank failures required stronger regulation, not simply wishing for prevention. All three agreed that stronger rules were needed.

USA.title: White House plans tougher midsize-bank rules recommendation
USA.summary: According to people familiar with the matter, the White House planned to recommend tougher midsize-bank rules from the Federal Reserve and other agencies following the failures of Silicon Valley Bank and Signature Bank. Recommendations covering banks with $100 billion to $250 billion in assets were expected as soon as that week. The Fed was already considering stronger capital, liquidity and stress-testing requirements. The White House declined to comment.

USA.title: Biden calls for stronger bank rules after SVB failure
USA.summary: Following Silicon Valley Bank’s failure, President Joe Biden publicly pledged to ask Congress and banking regulators, including the Federal Reserve in its supervisory role, to strengthen bank rules to reduce the risk of similar failures and protect American jobs and small businesses. He also assured depositors that their funds would be protected without losses falling on taxpayers. The linked report does not date his remarks; its publication date is used.

USA.title: Elizabeth Warren warns Fed tightening risks millions of jobs
USA.summary: Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren criticized the employment risks of the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate increases in questioning reported during Jerome Powell’s semiannual congressional testimony, warning that its policies could leave millions of people without jobs. Powell said further increases could be appropriate at a slower pace and acknowledged that tighter credit conditions would likely weigh on hiring and economic activity.

USA.title: Yellen opposes debating inflation target change now
USA.summary: In a Bloomberg interview, US Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen opposed debating a change to the Federal Reserve's inflation target at that time. She said core inflation remained quite high and some slowdown in consumer spending was probably needed to bring inflation under control. Her position aligned with Fed Chair Jerome Powell's rejection of reconsidering the 2% target.

USA.title: Biden calls for stronger bank rules after SVB collapse
USA.summary: Responding to Silicon Valley Bank’s collapse, US President Joe Biden said he would ask Congress and banking regulators, including the Federal Reserve, to strengthen bank rules to reduce the risk of similar failures and protect American jobs and small businesses. He also assured depositors that their funds would be protected without losses falling on taxpayers. The linked retrospective does not establish the date of his remarks.

USA.title: DeSantis says he would replace Powell as Fed chair
USA.summary: Florida governor and Republican presidential candidate Ron DeSantis said on Monday that, if elected president, he would seek to replace Federal Reserve chair Jay Powell, potentially before Powell’s term expires in 2026. The reported statement did not specify a monetary policy direction.

USA.title: Ron DeSantis criticizes Fed-controlled digital dollar
USA.summary: In a recorded statement played on the FT News Briefing, Republican presidential candidate and Florida governor Ron DeSantis criticized a Federal Reserve-controlled digital dollar, alleging that authorities would use it to impose an ESG agenda and block purchases such as gasoline deemed excessive. The discussion noted that there was no evidence of central banks planning to stop particular purchases. The recording's original date was not established.

USA.title: Republican senators challenge Fed capital requirements in letter
USA.summary: Republican senators on the Senate Banking Committee wrote to the Federal Reserve questioning whether it should pursue the proposed Basel III endgame capital requirements. The letter was recalled in a December 2 report ahead of the committee’s annual oversight hearing with major bank CEOs, amid Republican opposition to higher capital requirements. The report did not specify when the letter was sent.

USA.title: Trump voices preference for low interest rates
USA.summary: Former US president Donald Trump voiced a preference for low interest rates and less regulation, advocating an easier policy direction for the Federal Reserve. A January 22 report credited his remarks with helping lift small-cap stocks that day, even as investors pushed back expectations for Fed rate cuts. No threat or institutional change was reported.

USA.title: Trump says he would not reappoint Powell as Fed chair
USA.summary: Donald Trump said he would not reappoint Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and supplied a list of preferred replacements, describing them as more open. The report presented these remarks as raising concerns about the Fed’s autonomy, but did not establish a specific monetary-policy demand or the date of Trump’s remarks.

USA.title: Trump allies propose presidential oversight of Fed decisions
USA.summary: A group of Donald Trump's allies drafted proposals to curb Federal Reserve independence under a potential second Trump administration. Their plan called for presidential consultation on interest-rate decisions and White House review of Fed regulations, and suggested removing Jerome Powell as chair before his term ended while retaining him as a governor. The group argued that an elected president should influence monetary policy. Trump's knowledge or approval could not be established; his senior advisers said only proposals coming directly from Trump or his campaign were official. Some Republican lawmakers opposed challenges to Fed independence.

USA.title: Trump calls Fed overly stringent
USA.summary: In an archival statement replayed in an April 30, 2024 podcast, then-President Donald Trump criticized the Federal Reserve as “far too stringent,” saying it was “making a mistake” and its approach was “not right.” The statement advocated looser policy amid his first-term conflict with Fed Chair Jerome Powell over interest-rate increases. The story places the criticism in a campaign beginning in 2018 but does not establish the statement’s exact date.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Powell's performance
USA.summary: In an archival statement replayed in an April 30, 2024 podcast, Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell during his first presidency, saying, “I'm not happy with his actions” and “I don't think he's done a good job.” The statement questioned Powell's performance but contained no explicit policy demand or tenure threat. The linked story does not establish the original statement's exact date.

USA.title: Trump asks whether Powell or Xi is the bigger enemy
USA.summary: During his first term, President Donald Trump asked on Twitter whether Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell or Chinese President Xi Jinping was the bigger enemy of the United States. The post escalated his public criticism of Powell amid a dispute over interest rates, but the cited statement contained no explicit policy demand or threat of removal. The linked retrospective does not establish the post's exact date.

USA.title: Trump casts pre-election Fed cuts as pro-Biden interference
USA.summary: Former president and presidential candidate Donald Trump characterized a potential Federal Reserve rate cut before the election as part of a pro-Biden “deep state” operation, challenging the Fed’s political neutrality. The linked report provides no specific date for his remarks. It also recounts Chair Jerome Powell’s statement that the Fed does not consider elections when making policy decisions.

USA.title: Trump threatens to fire Powell if reelected
USA.summary: The FT News Briefing reported that presidential candidate Donald Trump threatened to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell if reelected, regardless of whether he had legal authority to do so. According to the discussion, Trump viewed Powell, whom he appointed, as having betrayed him. The reported removal threat did not establish a specific policy demand.

USA.title: Senate bill seeks to bar a digital dollar
USA.summary: A bill introduced in the US Senate in February 2024 sought to prohibit a digital dollar, placing a proposed statutory restriction on the Federal Reserve's ability to introduce a central bank digital currency. The report does not identify the sponsors or exact introduction date. The Fed was exploring the technology but had said it would not proceed without broad political and public support.

USA.title: DeSantis bans CBDCs in Florida
USA.summary: Florida Governor Ron DeSantis banned central bank digital currencies in his state in 2023, opposing a potential digital dollar being explored by the Federal Reserve. The linked report does not specify the ban's exact date. It also reports that the Fed would not proceed with a digital dollar without broad political and public support.

USA.title: Trump advisers draft plan to end Fed independence
USA.summary: Reporting described Donald Trump's advisers drafting a proposal to undermine the Federal Reserve's traditional independence by having its chair regularly consult the president about interest rates and giving the president a voice in those decisions. The Trump campaign characterized the proposal as unofficial. The discussion linked it to Trump's preference for low rates, but did not establish a specific rate demand in the draft.

USA.title: Democrats warn Powell against delaying rate cuts
USA.summary: During Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s semi-annual congressional testimony, Democratic lawmakers warned that delaying interest-rate cuts could harm the economy, citing rising unemployment, elevated housing costs and slowing manufacturing. Powell acknowledged that the labour market had cooled and that inflation was not the only economic risk, but said more data were needed and gave no timetable for cuts.

USA.title: Trump allies draft plan for presidential control of Fed
USA.summary: Close allies of Donald Trump reportedly drafted a plan to bring the Federal Reserve under greater presidential control if he were elected, reducing its independence. The linked story cites an April 2024 Wall Street Journal report but provides no exact date or advocated monetary-policy direction. It notes that the Fed remained independent at the time of the July report.

USA.title: Trump urges no Fed rate cuts before election in Bloomberg interview
USA.summary: In a Bloomberg Businessweek interview conducted before his debate with President Biden, Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump urged the Federal Reserve not to cut interest rates before the November election, implying that cuts would benefit Biden politically. Asked about removing Jerome Powell, Trump said he would let Powell complete his term, conditional on his "doing things right." The linked reports do not establish the interview's exact date. Powell subsequently stressed that the Fed follows its price-stability and full-employment mandate.

USA.title: Trump calls for presidential say over the Fed
USA.summary: At an August 8 press conference, former US president and Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump said the president should have a say in Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions, advocating greater political influence over the independent central bank. He criticized the timing of Fed decisions and claimed his business experience gave him better instincts than many Fed officials. He did not specify how presidential input would be implemented or advocate a particular rate direction in these remarks. Fed Chair Jerome Powell had pledged not to let political pressure influence policy decisions.

USA.title: Trump calls pre-election rate cut a gift to Democrats
USA.summary: Former president and presidential candidate Donald Trump said that any Federal Reserve interest rate cut before the November election would amount to a gift to Democrats, opposing a pre-election cut and questioning its political neutrality. The August 9 report dated his remarks only to several weeks earlier and reported that the Fed maintained its policy decisions were based on economic conditions, not the election.

USA.title: Harris pledges to respect Federal Reserve independence
USA.summary: Asked about Donald Trump's call for presidential influence over interest rates and monetary policy, Vice President and Democratic presidential candidate Kamala Harris said she could not disagree more strongly. She described the Federal Reserve as independent and pledged never to interfere in its decisions as president, without advocating a particular monetary policy direction.

USA.title: Kennedy presses Powell on rate-cut timing
USA.summary: During congressional questioning in July 2024, Republican Senator John Kennedy pressed Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on when he would lower interest rates. Powell declined to signal the timing of future actions. The linked report does not establish the exact date of the exchange.

USA.title: Vance backs electoral control over interest-rate policy
USA.summary: In weekend comments reported on August 14, 2024, Republican vice-presidential candidate JD Vance backed presidential input into Federal Reserve monetary policy. He argued that voters dissatisfied with interest-rate policy should be able to elect someone to change it and that major national questions should remain open to democratic debate, challenging the Fed’s policy autonomy without advocating a specific interest-rate direction.

USA.title: Trump opposes Fed rate cuts ahead of election
USA.summary: Donald Trump opposed Federal Reserve interest-rate cuts ahead of the election, saying a cut would be unfair and would benefit Biden and Harris. Recalling the undated statement in Bloomberg's September 14 preview of the Fed meeting, correspondent Michael McKee countered that a cut would not materially affect the economy until the following year.

USA.title: Trump questions economic health after Fed rate cut
USA.summary: Following the Federal Reserve’s half-percentage-point interest-rate cut, Donald Trump countered that the decision indicated the US economy was in worse condition than previously thought. His reported response did not advocate a particular policy direction or threaten action against the Fed.

USA.title: Trump proposes changing the Fed's governing law
USA.summary: Donald Trump was recalled as having proposed changing the law governing the Federal Reserve during campaign remarks. An October 14, 2024 discussion described the unspecified legal changes as a potential source of initial market anxiety if he won. The account establishes neither a specific monetary policy direction nor the date of Trump's remarks.

USA.title: Trump signals he would not reappoint Powell
USA.summary: A Bloomberg HT discussion recalled Republican presidential candidate Donald Trump's earlier statement that he probably would not select Jerome Powell again to lead the Federal Reserve. The recalled statement signaled potential non-renewal but established no monetary policy demand. The story did not identify the statement's date.

USA.title: Trump calls for presidential say over Fed rates in Bloomberg interview
USA.summary: In a Bloomberg interview, US presidential candidate Donald Trump argued that the president should have a say in whether Federal Reserve interest rates rise or fall, advocating a presidential role in its independent policymaking without specifying a rate direction. He mocked Jerome Powell's chairmanship as the easiest government job, likening it to appearing monthly, flipping a coin and being treated like a god. In a later interview, ECB President Christine Lagarde defended central bankers' work and the importance of central-bank independence.

USA.title: Trump voices desire to dismiss Powell as presidential candidate
USA.summary: Presidential candidate Donald Trump was reported to have said he wanted to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, suggesting Powell was not doing a useful job. Linked discussions recalled the remark while considering how a Trump presidency could influence Fed decisions, with a later account describing replacement if Powell did not follow Trump's wishes. No specific policy direction or date for the original statement was established.

USA.title: Trump demands presidential say in Fed decisions
USA.summary: Donald Trump demanded that the US president have a say in Federal Reserve monetary policy decisions, challenging the bank’s institutional autonomy. November 7 reports recalled the demand without establishing its exact date. Fed Chair Jerome Powell had repeatedly stressed that the Fed was not a political body; accompanying analysis noted institutional safeguards against presidential interference.

USA.title: Trump signals desire for Fed input in Micklethwait interview
USA.summary: In a pre-election interview with Bloomberg's John Micklethwait, presidential candidate Donald Trump hinted that he wanted greater involvement in Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions. The linked report characterized his response on Fed independence as equivocal, rather than an explicit commitment to intervene. It established neither a preferred rate direction nor a threat to officials or institutional autonomy, and did not specify the interview date.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Fed's election-campaign half-point rate cut
USA.summary: During the US election campaign, Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for the Fed's 50-basis-point interest-rate cut, opposing that easing. The linked report recalls the criticism without establishing its exact date or reporting a threat attached to it.

USA.title: Trump advisers suggest asking Powell to resign
USA.summary: Some advisers to President-elect Donald Trump reportedly suggested asking Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to resign. No monetary-policy direction or date for the suggestion was established. Asked at a press conference whether he would leave if Trump requested it, Powell said no; he also said the law does not permit a president to fire or demote him.

USA.title: Trump announces intention to remove Powell
USA.summary: President-elect Donald Trump reportedly announced that he wanted to remove Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. The report described a potential confrontation, noting that removal would require strong legal grounds and that Powell had said he would not resign voluntarily if Trump asked him to.

USA.title: Trump seeks presidential seat at Fed table in summer Bloomberg interview
USA.summary: In a Bloomberg interview during summer 2024, Donald Trump said the president should have a seat at the Federal Reserve's table and greater involvement in determining interest rates. The demand challenged the separation of presidential fiscal policy and independent monetary policy, without specifying a direction for rates. The linked report does not establish the interview's exact date.

USA.title: Trump says he will not reappoint Powell
USA.summary: A Bloomberg HT discussion recalled Donald Trump saying he would not reappoint Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell when his term ends in 2026. The participants distinguished non-reappointment from voluntary resignation, noting Powell's stated refusal to resign. The report did not date Trump's statement or establish a policy demand attached to it.

USA.title: Trump mocks Powell's workload and rate decisions
USA.summary: In earlier remarks recalled in a November 19, 2024 broadcast, Donald Trump mocked Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell as having the world's best job: working once a month, tossing a coin to make decisions and then being treated like a god. The remarks disparaged Powell's work and policy judgment without advocating a specific policy direction. The broadcast also recalled Christine Lagarde inviting Trump to Frankfurt to see how central banks work. The date of Trump's remarks was not established.

USA.title: Carter endorses Volcker's tough anti-inflation approach
USA.summary: According to a retrospective account of Paul Volcker's 1979 nomination as Federal Reserve chairman, President Jimmy Carter endorsed Volcker's proposed substantial interest-rate increases to fight inflation despite warnings of recession and job losses. Carter told Volcker to handle the economy and inflation, supporting his policy autonomy with reelection approaching. The account does not establish the precise date of their exchange.

USA.title: Trump says interest rates are too high
USA.summary: Donald Trump said interest rates were too high on January 7, 2025, according to Bloomberg HT commentators speaking the following day. They discussed his remark as pressure on the Federal Reserve to lower rates amid rising US Treasury yields and reduced market expectations for rate cuts.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Fed's authority over monetary policy
USA.summary: In remarks recalled during a January 15, 2025 Bloomberg HT discussion, Donald Trump questioned the Federal Reserve’s authority, complaining that Jerome Powell and other Fed officials met every month or two and dictated decisions on matters for which he bore political responsibility, preventing him from doing what he wanted. The recalled remarks challenged the institutional arrangement but specified neither a policy direction nor a concrete institutional change. The date of Trump’s original remarks was not established.

USA.title: Bessent floats shadow Fed chair proposal
USA.summary: Scott Bessent, identified as Donald Trump's likely Treasury secretary, had floated creating a shadow Federal Reserve chair. A January 18 inauguration discussion recalled the proposal as potentially undermining incumbent Chair Jerome Powell's authority, while expressing uncertainty that it would happen. The report established neither a monetary-policy demand nor the date of Bessent's proposal.

USA.title: Trump demands immediate rate cuts in Davos speech
USA.summary: In a video address to the World Economic Forum in Davos, US President Donald Trump said he would ask Saudi Arabia and OPEC to lower oil prices and demand that interest rates fall immediately as oil prices declined. His call pressured the Federal Reserve to ease policy and extended to rates worldwide. On January 29, the Fed held rates unchanged, and Chair Jerome Powell declined to comment on Trump's remarks.

USA.title: Trump's past threat to remove Powell recalled
USA.summary: In reports published on January 24, 2025, interviewers and a correspondent recalled Donald Trump's past threat to remove Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over interest-rate policy disagreements during Trump's first term. No specific date or advocated policy direction was established for that threat. Economist William Lee said the president could not remove a Fed governor but could appoint the next chair; the Bloomberg correspondent noted that Powell was not fired.

USA.title: Trump seeks input on Fed policy in Micklethwait interview
USA.summary: In an October interview with Bloomberg editor-in-chief John Micklethwait, Donald Trump said he should be able to weigh in on Federal Reserve interest-rate policy, while acknowledging the Fed's independence and saying he should not make the decisions himself. The linked account does not establish the interview's exact date or a preferred interest-rate direction.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Fed inflation record after rate hold
USA.summary: After the Federal Reserve held interest rates steady, US President Donald Trump criticized it in a Truth Social post, saying Powell and the Fed had failed to stop inflation they had created and that he would solve it. He argued that rates should fall and alleged that the Fed's attention to gender ideology, diversity initiatives and climate issues had distracted it from fighting inflation. Powell said the Fed was in no hurry to adjust rates and declined to comment on Trump's remarks.

USA.title: Trump claims to understand interest rates better than Powell
USA.summary: President Donald Trump claimed that he understood interest rates better than Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, questioning Powell’s judgment without advocating a specific policy direction in the reported remarks. The January 30 report recalled the statement without identifying its date or occasion. At the Fed’s subsequent press conference, Powell said he had not been in contact with Trump and declined to comment on his criticism.

USA.title: Trump disparages Fed chairmanship as an easy job
USA.summary: In earlier remarks recalled in a January 30, 2025 broadcast, Donald Trump disparaged the Federal Reserve chairmanship as an exceptionally easy job. He said the chair meets roughly every month and a half, makes one decision and then enjoys widespread respect without other responsibilities. The account does not date these remarks or attribute a policy demand or institutional threat to them.

USA.title: Trump order subjects Fed regulation to presidential oversight
USA.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order in mid-February 2025 subjecting the Federal Reserve's spending, financial regulation and supervision to tighter presidential oversight while explicitly exempting monetary policy. A senior administration official said the Office of Management and Budget would oversee all Fed regulations unrelated to monetary policy. The administration denied that the order would erode the credibility of the Fed's interest-rate decisions. The linked report does not establish the exact signing date.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Fed banking regulation
USA.summary: In a January 2025 statement, President Donald Trump said the Federal Reserve was doing a “terrible job” on banking regulations, criticizing its performance as a bank regulator. The linked report does not establish the statement’s exact date or identify a specific policy demand or threat attached to it.

USA.title: Trump calls for interest-rate cuts
USA.summary: A March 4 podcast discussion reported that US President Donald Trump had requested interest-rate cuts from the Federal Reserve, without identifying the occasion of his request. The demand was mentioned amid falling Treasury yields and expectations that tariff-related economic weakness could prompt Fed rate cuts. No threat or Fed response was reported.

USA.title: Trump urges rate cuts as tariffs are introduced
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump urged the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates following its decision to wait for further inflation progress and clarity on his trade policies. He said the Fed would be much better off cutting rates as tariffs were introduced. The Fed had lowered its growth projections, raised its inflation forecast and continued to project half a percentage point of rate cuts during 2025.

USA.title: Biden urges Federal Reserve to explore a digital dollar
USA.summary: In a 2022 executive order, US President Joe Biden urged the Federal Reserve to begin studying and developing a digital dollar. The story attributes the initiative to concern that the United States could fall behind China, which was already testing its digital currency. It provides no exact date for Biden's order.

USA.title: Trump prohibits development of a digital dollar
USA.summary: President Donald Trump issued a decree on January 23, 2025, prohibiting development of a digital dollar and reversing Biden's initiative for Federal Reserve exploration. The prohibition restricted the Fed's scope to develop a central bank digital currency. The report placed it in the context of Republican concerns that such a currency could enable mass government control.

USA.title: Trump urges rate cut ahead of Powell's Virginia remarks
USA.summary: President Donald Trump urged Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on Truth Social to cut interest rates and stop playing politics ahead of Powell’s April 4 remarks in Virginia. Powell warned that tariff increases could produce higher inflation and slower growth and said the Fed was well positioned to wait for greater clarity before changing policy.

USA.title: Trump tells Powell to cut rates and stop playing politics
USA.summary: In an all-capitals Truth Social post, US President Donald Trump called the situation a major win for the United States and demanded that Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell lower interest rates and stop playing politics. The accusation came amid tariff-related market turmoil and concerns about inflation and weaker growth. Later coverage cited the remarks as raising concerns about coordination between the administration and the Fed during a crisis. The linked reports do not establish the post's exact date.

USA.title: Trump asks Chief Justice Roberts about firing Powell
USA.summary: An April 11 broadcast reported that President Donald Trump had asked Chief Justice John Roberts whether he could fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. The discussion linked the inquiry to rumors of hedge-fund losses and a possible Fed rescue, speculating that Trump could use such intervention as a pretext to remove Powell. It established no specific policy demand or removal action.

USA.title: Trump calls for Powell's termination and rate cuts on Truth Social
USA.summary: In a morning Truth Social post on April 17, 2025, US President Donald Trump said Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's termination "cannot come fast enough," called him "always too late and wrong," and urged the Fed to cut interest rates as other central banks had done. The post followed Powell's warning the previous day that tariffs could raise prices and weaken economic growth.

USA.title: Trump threatens to remove Powell at Oval Office press conference
USA.summary: At an Oval Office press conference with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for being too slow to lower interest rates and urged the Fed to follow the ECB in cutting rates. Responding to a question about Powell refusing to leave, Trump said, “If I ask him to, he'll be out of there,” and asserted he could remove him “real fast.” Trump said he had communicated his dissatisfaction to Powell. The reporting noted that Fed governors can legally be removed only for cause.

USA.title: Hassett says Powell's removal is under study
USA.summary: Responding to a reporter on April 18, National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett said the administration was studying whether President Trump could dismiss Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. His statement raised the prospect of Powell’s removal without itself advocating a monetary-policy direction. Powell had maintained that the law protected him from removal without cause. Trump subsequently said on April 22 that he had no intention of firing Powell.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell a big loser on Monday
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump attacked Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on Truth Social, calling him a “major loser” and “Mr. Too Late” and demanding immediate interest-rate cuts. Trump claimed there was almost no inflation and warned of an economic slowdown without cuts. The Fed had been waiting because of uncertainty about tariffs’ inflationary effects. The attack accompanied sharp declines in US stocks and the dollar, amid concerns about Fed independence following separate earlier discussions of Powell’s removal.

USA.title: Trump claims power to dismiss Powell during Meloni visit
USA.summary: During Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's White House visit, President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for not cutting interest rates and asserted that he could dismiss him at any time, saying Powell would be gone very quickly if he wanted him out. The report disputed Trump's claimed dismissal power and linked the threat to concerns about Federal Reserve independence and investor confidence. The linked story does not establish the visit's exact date.

USA.title: Trump disavows firing Powell but urges rate cuts
USA.summary: Responding to reporters in the Oval Office, US President Donald Trump said he had no intention of firing Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and denied ever intending to do so. He nevertheless urged Powell to be more active in lowering interest rates, calling it the perfect time for cuts, while saying that failure to cut would not be the end. The remarks softened his earlier rhetoric about Powell’s removal and were followed by gains in stocks and the dollar.

USA.title: White House lawyers examine options to remove Powell
USA.summary: White House lawyers reportedly examined options for removing Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell amid President Trump's threats to fire him. The reporting did not establish whether a legal route to removal existed. Trump subsequently said he had no intention of firing Powell.

USA.title: Trump tells reporters Powell will leave quickly if he wants
USA.summary: Speaking to journalists, US President Donald Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and said that if he wanted Powell to leave, he would leave quickly. The statement threatened Powell’s tenure and asserted presidential power to remove him despite the legal protections for Federal Reserve independence described in the report.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Powell at Michigan 100-day rally
USA.summary: At a Michigan rally marking his first 100 days back in office, US President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell as "not really doing a good job" and claimed to know more about interest rates than Powell. Trump said inflation and interest rates had fallen despite Powell, but did not explicitly demand a policy change or renew his earlier threats to dismiss him.

USA.title: White House lawyers explore authority to remove Powell
USA.summary: According to a Wall Street Journal report recalled in a May 4 interview, White House lawyers explored whether President Trump could remove Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell before his term ended in 2026. The report was described only as occurring a few weeks earlier. Trump subsequently said he had no intention of firing Powell.

USA.title: Trump renews pressure for Fed rate cuts over weekend
USA.summary: President Donald Trump renewed pressure on the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates over the weekend preceding May 5, 2025, according to a Norwegian broadcast. The report did not quote his remarks or specify their venue or exact date.

USA.title: Bessent reportedly secures conditional Fed rate-cut agreement
USA.summary: A May 6 podcast claimed that US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent met weekly with Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and had secured an agreement for rate cuts if the 10-year Treasury yield remained above a threshold for an extended period. The transcript does not clearly establish the threshold. The speaker characterized the alleged arrangement as politically directed monetary policy and warned it would hurt the dollar; the story provided no confirmation from Bessent or the Fed.

USA.title: Trump tells reporters he could remove Powell quickly
USA.summary: In remarks to reporters in April 2025, President Donald Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and threatened rapid removal: "If I want him out, he'll be out of there real fast, believe me." The story places his dissatisfaction in the context of his demands for lower interest rates and complaints that Powell was cutting too slowly. Powell has maintained that the president cannot legally fire him. The precise date of the remarks is not established.

USA.title: Trump urges Fed to follow ECB rate cuts
USA.summary: In April 2025, President Donald Trump urged the Federal Reserve and Chair Jerome Powell to follow the European Central Bank's example and cut interest rates. The May 8 report recalled the intervention without specifying its exact date. It also reported Powell's view that waiting would help the Fed assess tariffs' potentially conflicting effects on inflation and growth.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell slow and stupid after Fed holds rates
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump attacked Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell after the Fed left interest rates unchanged, pressing for lower rates. Trump described Powell as slow, stupid and incompetent, and called him a fool who did not have a clue. The reports contrasted Trump's demands with Powell's position that economic conditions must justify rate cuts.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell a loser
USA.summary: President Donald Trump called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell a “loser” amid pressure for lower interest rates to stimulate the US economy. The linked reports recall the remark without dating it, separately from Trump's subsequent criticism calling Powell a fool; the date reflects the reports' publication date.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell a fool who lacks a clue
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell a “fool who doesn't have a clue,” continuing his pressure for lower interest rates to stimulate the economy. The criticism followed the Fed's decision to keep rates unchanged and Powell's indication that it would wait for greater clarity on tariffs' price effects before acting.

USA.title: Trump demands rate cuts after April inflation report
USA.summary: Following lower-than-expected April inflation figures, US President Donald Trump demanded that the Federal Reserve cut interest rates as Europe and China had done. He claimed there was no inflation and that gasoline, energy, groceries and practically everything else were falling in price, and criticized Chair Jerome Powell by asking, "What is wrong with too late Powell?"

USA.title: Trump criticizes Powell's rate hold at White House meeting
USA.summary: At their first White House meeting of Trump's second term, President Donald Trump told Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell that he was making a mistake by not lowering interest rates. The meeting took place at Trump's invitation. The Fed said Powell did not discuss specific monetary-policy expectations and stressed that interest-rate decisions would depend on economic data.

USA.title: Trump urges rate cuts after weak ADP jobs report
USA.summary: President Donald Trump urged Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to lower interest rates in a Truth Social post after ADP reported that private employers added just 37,000 jobs in May, the weakest growth in more than two years. The Fed had reiterated the previous week that its rate decisions rest solely on careful, objective and nonpolitical analysis.

USA.title: Trump calls for a full percentage-point rate cut
USA.summary: Donald Trump called on Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to lower interest rates by one full percentage point. A Bloomberg interview published June 6, 2025, reported that he made the demand the previous week, without establishing an exact date. The interview contrasted his call with inflation risks that could keep the Fed from cutting rates.

USA.title: Trump says a good Fed chair would cut rates
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump said that a good Federal Reserve chair would cut interest rates, linking the chair’s competence to monetary easing. The remark was reported during a discussion of US–China trade talks and uncertainty over tariffs, inflation and the Fed’s policy outlook.

USA.title: Trump urges one-point rate cut after May CPI release
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called on the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates by one percentage point in a social-media post following the release of May inflation figures. Calling the figures “great,” he urged easing ahead of the Fed’s meeting the following week. Annual headline inflation was 2.4% and underlying inflation was 2.8%; coverage noted uncertainty about the inflationary effects of tariffs.

USA.title: Trump names Scott Bessent as his next Fed chair candidate
USA.summary: According to the June 12 report, President Donald Trump named Scott Bessent as his candidate for the next Federal Reserve chair earlier that week, although Jerome Powell's term would not expire until May 2026. The commentator characterized the advance announcement as pressure on Powell and Fed independence. The report did not establish the exact announcement date.

USA.title: Trump blasts anticipated Fed hold and demands deeper rate cuts
USA.summary: On June 18, 2025, before the Federal Reserve's rate decision, US President Donald Trump criticized its anticipated hold, called Chair Jerome Powell "stupid," and demanded substantially lower interest rates. Reports differed on the size of the cut sought. Trump argued that inflation was absent and lower rates would strengthen the economy. The Fed held rates steady, with Powell citing expected tariff-related inflation and uncertainty as reasons for patience.

USA.title: Trump publicly discusses Powell replacement and calls him terrible
USA.summary: Speaking publicly at the NATO summit, US President Donald Trump said he had narrowed his choice of successor to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to three or four people. He called Powell “terrible,” welcomed his approaching departure and asserted that the United States had no inflation and a tremendous economy, amid pressure for lower interest rates. Trump named no candidates or decision timeline; Powell’s chairmanship was due to expire in May 2026.

USA.title: Trump weighs early successor announcement to sideline Powell
USA.summary: A Wall Street Journal report said US President Donald Trump was considering announcing Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s successor in autumn 2025, well before Powell’s term ends in May 2026. The prospective nominee was described as a 'shadow chair' favouring faster interest-rate cuts, potentially pressuring Powell and weakening his authority. Linked coverage warned that competing policy signals could confuse markets and undermine Fed credibility, while noting that an incoming chair would not necessarily sway other monetary policymakers. No early nomination was reported as completed.

USA.title: Trump says Powell is not doing his job by withholding rate cuts
USA.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, saying he was not doing his job because he had not lowered interest rates. The June 26 remarks pressed for rate cuts and challenged Powell’s performance. Linked coverage described Powell as maintaining that the Fed would follow the data.

USA.title: Bessent discusses options for positioning Powell's successor
USA.summary: Answering Bloomberg’s questions, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent outlined two options for Federal Reserve chair succession: appointing a prospective successor to an upcoming vacant governor seat before Jerome Powell’s chair term expires, or choosing a current governor closer to President Trump’s views. The report suggested the first option could weaken Powell’s standing and accelerate rate cuts, but did not attribute that policy demand to Bessent.

USA.title: Trump calls for Powell's immediate resignation
USA.summary: President Donald Trump demanded Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's immediate resignation after the housing finance agency director alleged that Powell had misled the Senate about luxury features in a roughly $2.5 billion Fed building renovation project. The director also raised the possibility of an investigation. The resignation demand came amid Trump's broader pressure for interest-rate cuts, but this intervention concerned the renovation allegations rather than an explicit monetary-policy demand.

USA.title: Housing finance agency director accuses Powell of misleading Senate
USA.summary: In a statement, the US housing finance agency director accused Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell of misleading the Senate by downplaying luxury features in a roughly $2.5 billion Fed building renovation project. The director said Powell could face an investigation. The intervention did not specify a monetary policy demand or call for Powell’s removal.

USA.title: Trump urges Powell to cut rates by one percentage point
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump urged Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to cut interest rates by one percentage point, saying Powell was behind in easing monetary policy. The linked reports recall the demand without identifying its original occasion or date; July 7 is the earliest report date.

USA.title: Bessent advocates waiting until autumn to name a new Fed chair
USA.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was reported as advocating waiting until October or November to appoint a new Federal Reserve chair, with a January 1 start, and urging against rushing the replacement. The commentator linked this timing to forecasts of falling inflation early the following year; that explanation was not presented as Bessent’s explicit statement.

USA.title: Trump says he will appoint a Fed chair who will cut rates
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump said he would appoint a Federal Reserve chair who would cut interest rates. Bloomberg HT discussions on July 7 and 8 recalled the remarks without identifying their occasion or original date. A commentator said the remarks made rate cuts appear to be the sole appointment criterion, while suggesting other criteria would likely apply. No explicit removal threat or institutional change was reported.

USA.title: Trump calls for interest rates near zero or one percent
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called for Federal Reserve interest rates of zero or one percent, arguing that low rates would help the government service its debt. The July 8 discussion distinguished this demand from his earlier call for a one-percentage-point cut; July 10 coverage reiterated his preference for a one-percent rate. Neither story identifies the occasion or exact date of the remarks.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell terrible and demands immediate rate cuts
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell "terrible" and accused him of "whining like a baby about non-existent inflation for months" and refusing to do the right thing. Trump demanded immediate monetary easing, saying, "Cut interest rates, Jerome, now is the time."

USA.title: Pulte requests congressional investigation and Powell resignation
USA.summary: Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte requested a congressional investigation into whether Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell had lied to lawmakers about the Fed’s headquarters renovation and demanded his resignation. The allegation concerned testimony about the renovation, whose rising costs and reportedly extravagant features had drawn scrutiny. Powell had previously disputed descriptions of the project as misleading and inaccurate.

USA.title: Trump demands Powell resign if testimony allegations are true
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump echoed Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte’s allegations on social media, saying Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell should resign immediately if he had lied to Congress about the Fed’s headquarters renovation. The allegation was not established in the report. Powell had previously rejected reports of extravagant renovation features as misleading and inaccurate.

USA.title: Trump raises Powell's removal over testimony at cabinet meeting
USA.summary: At a July 8 cabinet meeting, U.S. President Donald Trump called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell “terrible” and said misleading Congress would justify his swift departure, referring to allegations concerning testimony about Fed headquarters renovations. Trump also endorsed appointing someone who would lower interest rates and told Treasury Secretary Scott Bessant he liked him better than Powell. Powell had previously rejected reports about extravagant renovation features as misleading and inaccurate.

USA.title: Trump says Powell's termination cannot come fast enough
USA.summary: In an April 2025 social media post, US President Donald Trump wrote that Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's “termination cannot come fast enough,” raising the prospect of removing him. Trump subsequently said he could get Powell to leave the next day if he wanted, but days later denied seriously considering removal. The linked story does not establish the post's exact date.

USA.title: Trump says he could make Powell leave tomorrow
USA.summary: Asked about firing Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell following an April 2025 social media post, President Donald Trump said he could get Powell to leave "tomorrow" if he wanted. The remarks raised market concerns about Powell's potential dismissal. The linked report says Trump backed down a few days later, denying he had seriously considered firing Powell, but does not establish the exact date of the remarks.

USA.title: White House calls for Fed policy to complement Trump's agenda
USA.summary: In a statement addressing President Trump's search for a Federal Reserve chair, a White House spokesman said Fed monetary policy needed to complement the administration's pro-growth agenda. He added that Trump would continue nominating the most qualified individuals to serve Americans. The statement did not specify an interest-rate change or threaten removal or institutional changes.

USA.title: Hassett accuses Powell of politically driven rate decisions
USA.summary: In a Fox Business interview with Maria Bartiromo, White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett accused Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell of politically driven policy decisions. He alleged that Powell cut rates before the election to help Kamala Harris and supported raising rates before Donald Trump's first inauguration, suggesting Powell's actions followed Elizabeth Warren's wishes. Powell rejected accusations that the Fed behaves politically. The July 10 report placed the interview in the preceding few weeks without establishing an exact date.

USA.title: Besant urges Powell to leave Fed board after chair term
USA.summary: In a Bloomberg Television interview, Treasury Secretary Scott Besant said the search for the next Federal Reserve chair was underway and suggested Jerome Powell should also leave the Fed’s board when his chairmanship ends in May 2026, rather than remain as a governor. Besant said President Trump was not seeking to remove Powell before his chair term expired. This intervention did not advocate a specific monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Trump calls on Fed to cut rates on social media
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called on the Federal Reserve on social media to cut interest rates despite inflation rising to its highest level since February. The report contrasted his demand with Fed Chair Jerome Powell's stated preference to wait for evidence of tariffs' effects before changing rates.

USA.title: Trump raises possible removal for renovation fraud and demands rate cuts
USA.summary: Answering reporters at the White House, US President Donald Trump denied plans to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell but said he ruled nothing out and could remove him if fraud were involved in the Fed’s building renovations. He criticized the reported $2.5–$2.7 billion cost, alleged missing clearance, said Powell was doing a poor job and demanded lower interest rates. The linked reporting established no evidence of fraud. Trump also said he was considering economic adviser Kevin Hassett as Powell’s successor.

USA.title: Trump polls Republican lawmakers on firing Powell
USA.summary: During a closed-door White House meeting with Republican lawmakers, President Donald Trump asked whether he should fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell. Trump later said almost all participants supported removal, and a senior administration official said he suggested he could act in the near future. Trump subsequently denied planning to fire Powell, describing removal as highly unlikely unless fraud were involved; the linked reporting established no evidence of fraud.

USA.title: Johnson demands rate cuts in ranch confrontation
USA.summary: In a historical anecdote recounted in a July 17, 2025 broadcast, President Lyndon B. Johnson reportedly summoned a Federal Reserve chair, identified in the account as Burns, to his ranch and demanded interest-rate cuts. Johnson reportedly cited his difficulties with the Vietnam War and said he did not need additional problems. The account provides no date for the confrontation and describes no explicit tenure or institutional threat.

USA.title: Trump asks Republican lawmakers about removing Powell
USA.summary: President Donald Trump asked Republican lawmakers during an Oval Office meeting whether Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell should be removed; they reportedly supported the idea. The discussion came amid Trump's dissatisfaction with Powell for not cutting interest rates. Trump later said he was not planning to act unless fraud was involved, suggesting that was possible without evidence. Senior bankers defended Powell and Federal Reserve independence.

USA.title: Trump leaves Powell removal open over alleged fraud
USA.summary: Following an Oval Office meeting with Republican lawmakers, US President Donald Trump said he was not planning to remove Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell unless fraud was involved, adding that this was possible. The reporting presented no evidence of fraud. His conditional removal warning came amid scrutiny of the Fed headquarters renovation and broader pressure on Powell; senior bankers publicly defended the Fed's independence.

USA.title: Senate Republicans question Powell over headquarters renovation
USA.summary: At a congressional hearing in June 2025, Senate Republicans challenged Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the high costs, budget overruns and purported luxury finishes of the Fed’s headquarters renovation. Powell disputed the accuracy of reports about the finishes. The linked report does not establish the hearing’s exact date or identify a monetary-policy demand or threat by the senators.

USA.title: White House letter challenges Powell's renovation testimony
USA.summary: In a letter sent the week before July 17, 2025, the White House questioned Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell about the Fed headquarters renovation, suggesting his congressional testimony might have been untruthful and design plans might not have been properly updated with local authorities. The Fed maintained that Powell had been truthful and attributed cost overruns partly to unforeseen construction conditions.

USA.title: House passes bill to prohibit a digital dollar
USA.summary: The US House passed the Anti-CBDC Surveillance State Act on July 17, 2025, during Crypto Week. The legislation seeks to prohibit state issuance of a digital dollar, restricting the Federal Reserve’s digital-currency role. It passed alongside two other cryptocurrency bills as lawmakers pursued a framework encouraging private stablecoin issuance instead.

USA.title: Vought challenges Fed renovation costs and demands answers
USA.summary: U.S. Office of Management and Budget director Russell Vought criticized the Federal Reserve’s $2.5 billion historic-building renovation as ostentatious and demanded answers from Chair Jerome Powell. His questions appeared to suggest that Powell had misled Congress by not disclosing design changes. In a July 17 response, Powell said the Fed took its responsibility to steward public resources seriously. The report does not establish the exact date of Vought’s intervention.

USA.title: Trump says dismissing Powell is very unlikely
USA.summary: President Donald Trump denied on Wednesday that he was planning to dismiss Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, saying removal was very unlikely. His remarks followed reports that he might seek Powell’s removal, which contributed to market uncertainty. The denial itself contained no explicit policy demand or tenure threat.

USA.title: Trump raises firing Powell in closed-door meeting
USA.summary: President Donald Trump raised the possibility of firing Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell during a closed-door meeting on July 15, 2025. No specific policy demand was reported for that meeting. Trump denied the next day that he was planning to oust Powell. Reports linked uncertainty over Powell’s future to investor concern and weakness in financial-sector stocks.

USA.title: Bessent urges Trump not to fire Powell
USA.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent privately urged President Trump not to try to remove Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, arguing that the economy was holding up better than expected. He also warned that historical efforts to coordinate central banks with the Treasury to suppress government borrowing costs had produced substantial inflation. The report described the approach as occurring "this week" but did not establish an exact date.

USA.title: Bessent demands accounting of Fed building renovation
USA.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent demanded an explanation and itemized accounting of the Federal Reserve’s building renovation. The report characterized his demand as part of the Trump administration’s reputational pressure on Fed Chair Jerome Powell, raising suspicions of irregularities after efforts to remove Powell appeared unlikely to succeed. It did not establish wrongdoing or report a monetary-policy demand by Bessent in this intervention.

USA.title: House passes ban on Federal Reserve digital currency work
USA.summary: The US House of Representatives passed legislation prohibiting the Federal Reserve from creating or even studying a central bank digital currency in the week before July 23, 2025. Republicans justified their opposition by citing privacy concerns and the risk of government surveillance. The report does not establish the exact passage date or that the prohibition became law.

USA.title: Commerce Secretary calls for Powell to leave
USA.summary: The US Commerce Secretary said on July 23, 2025, that Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell should leave, according to a Bloomberg HT report published the following day. The report did not attribute a specific monetary-policy demand to the secretary.

USA.title: Bessent challenges Fed tariff analysis and urges institutional review
USA.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent challenged the Federal Reserve’s tariff analysis in an interview, arguing that tariffs had caused little price pressure and would produce a one-time adjustment rather than sustained inflation. He urged Chair Jerome Powell to review the institution and separate monetary policy from other functions, saying its expanding remit threatened monetary-policy independence. Bessent suggested a committee or outside experts could help, with an independent external review possible if the internal assessment lacked credibility. He did not call for Powell’s resignation.

USA.title: Trump visits Fed renovation site to pressure Powell
USA.summary: President Donald Trump toured the Federal Reserve headquarters renovation with Chair Jerome Powell, criticizing its costs and lengthy construction, regretting that it had started and urging completion. Amid his demands for lower interest rates, Trump called on Powell to do the right thing. Powell disputed Trump's $3.1 billion cost figure, saying it included a separate building completed five years earlier. Trump indicated he was not seeking to replace Powell.

USA.title: Tim Scott requests details on Fed renovation management
USA.summary: Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott sent Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell a letter requesting more details on management of the central bank’s $2.5 billion headquarters renovation. The request came a day before Scott accompanied President Trump on a tour of the construction site. No monetary-policy demand or threat was reported in Scott’s letter.

USA.title: Trump suggests renovation could justify firing Powell
USA.summary: In the week before his July 24, 2025 visit to the Federal Reserve, President Donald Trump suggested that its headquarters renovation might provide grounds to fire Chair Jerome Powell. The report described such a dismissal as unprecedented and legally questionable. The following day, Trump said removal was unlikely unless Powell had to leave for fraud; the story did not establish fraud. The initial statement’s exact date is not specified.

USA.title: Trump retains fraud exception to Powell removal restraint
USA.summary: President Donald Trump said he was unlikely to attempt to remove Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, but added, "unless he has to leave for fraud." The statement followed his suggestion the previous day that the Fed headquarters renovation could provide grounds for firing Powell. The exception preserved a conditional removal threat without establishing that fraud had occurred. The linked report places the remarks in the week before July 24 but does not establish an exact date.
