USA.title: Trump renews pressure on Powell to lower rates before Fed meeting
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump renewed his call for Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell to lower interest rates ahead of the Fed’s July meeting. Policymakers were assessing tariffs’ inflation effects, and most analysts expected no change. On July 30, the Fed kept rates at 4.25–4.5 percent, with two governors dissenting.

USA.title: Trump insults Powell in remarks before summit
USA.summary: Asked about his criticism of Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell before a summit, President Donald Trump called Powell terrible, very stupid and probably very political. He said Powell would leave fairly soon and welcomed that prospect, without explicitly threatening removal or advocating a policy change in these remarks. The comments came amid Trump's broader pressure for lower interest rates.

USA.title: Trump says unchanged rates cost billions annually
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump reiterated his demand that Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell lower interest rates, claiming that each percentage point not cut costs the United States $365 billion annually. That day, the Fed kept rates at 4.25–4.5% while awaiting greater clarity on the effects of Washington’s tariffs.

USA.title: Trump renews rate-cut call in post praising GDP growth
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump reiterated his call for Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell to lower interest rates in a social media post responding to preliminary figures showing 3% second-quarter US GDP growth. Trump praised the growth result as much better than expected.

USA.title: Trump challenges renovation costs during Fed visit
USA.summary: During a visit to the Federal Reserve’s renovation site, US President Donald Trump publicly challenged Chair Jerome Powell’s account of construction costs, accusing him of misrepresenting the expense and asserting a higher total. Powell disputed Trump’s figure, explaining that it included another building and a separate construction project. The linked reports do not unambiguously establish the visit’s date.

USA.title: Trump links Kugler departure to rates and promises replacement soon
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump told reporters he had a couple of candidates to replace departing Federal Reserve governor Adriana Kugler and would announce a nominee within days. He claimed she left early because she agreed with his preference for lower interest rates while others at the Fed opposed it; the reporting noted that this claim conflicted with her past public comments. Her departure opened an earlier-than-expected opportunity for Trump to appoint a governor aligned with his rate preferences.

USA.title: Hassett calls for transparency on Fed tariff-inflation forecasts
USA.summary: Appearing on Meet the Press, White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's transparency about expected tariff-driven inflation. He said Powell should present a model supporting that assessment to allow a substantive technical discussion. This intervention did not explicitly demand an interest-rate change or threaten Powell's tenure or the Fed's autonomy.

USA.title: Trump calls for three-percentage-point rate reduction
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called for interest rates to fall by three percentage points, according to an August 4 report that did not specify the occasion of his statement. His demand for Federal Reserve easing contrasted with market expectations of roughly one percentage point in cuts over the coming year.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell too angry, stupid and political
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell too angry, too stupid and too political, criticizing his persistent refusal to support lower interest rates. The report placed the remarks amid White House pressure for rate cuts and Trump's repeated calls for Powell's resignation, but did not establish that those resignation demands accompanied this particular intervention.

USA.title: Trump renews call for prompt rate cuts after weak jobs data
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump renewed his demand that the Federal Reserve and Chair Jerome Powell promptly cut interest rates after Friday's employment report showed weak hiring and substantial downward revisions to May and June job gains. The Fed had recently kept rates unchanged. Trump also criticized the employment data and called for dismissal of the head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics; that demand did not target Fed officials.

USA.title: Trump discusses installing a Fed critic in Kugler's vacant seat
USA.summary: In a CNBC interview, President Donald Trump discussed filling departing Federal Reserve governor Adriana Kugler’s seat with either his future Fed chair nominee or an interim appointee who could publicly criticize the Fed. He said he was considering four chair candidates, including Kevin Warsh and Kevin Hassett, and excluded Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent because Bessent wanted to remain in his current role. Trump did not announce an appointment or specify a policy direction for this intervention.

USA.title: Trump scrutinizes Fed construction during visit with Powell
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly challenged Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the Fed's construction project during a televised visit. The linked discussions described a dispute over project costs and footage of Powell holding a file and defending the work while Trump appeared not to listen. A commentator characterized the encounter as humiliating Powell and undermining the Fed's institutional standing. The stories do not establish the visit's exact date or a monetary-policy demand made during it.

USA.title: Trump nominates Steven Myron as Fed governor
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump nominated Council of Economic Advisers chair Steven Myron to the Federal Reserve Board seat vacated by Adriana Kugler, for a term ending in January 2026. Reports described him as an ally likely to support Trump's calls for aggressive interest-rate cuts. The temporary nomination gave Trump additional time to select a successor to Chair Jerome Powell. The Fed had kept rates on hold, partly over concerns about inflation from Trump's tariffs.

USA.title: Mirren dismisses tariff inflation concerns before Fed appointment
USA.summary: Trump economic adviser Stephen Mirren praised the president’s tariffs as historic and said there was “zero macroeconomically significant evidence of price pressures from the tariffs,” hours before his appointment to the Federal Reserve Board was announced. His remarks disputed tariff-inflation concerns cited as part of the Fed’s rationale for holding interest rates steady, without explicitly calling for a particular rate decision.

USA.title: Trump calls for rates three percentage points lower
USA.summary: Donald Trump called for Federal Reserve interest rates to be three percentage points below their current level. Recalling the demand in an August 11 discussion, Bloomberg HT commentators described it as an opening bargaining position and said neither the Fed nor markets supported such a radical reduction. They expected smaller, data-dependent cuts instead.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Powell during Fed construction-site visit
USA.summary: President Donald Trump berated Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell during a visit to the Fed's construction site, where both wore hard hats. Commentators recalling the visit described it as part of Trump's efforts to discredit Powell. The account provides no specific policy demand, tenure threat or exact date for the visit.

USA.title: Bessent urges openness to a half-point Fed rate cut
USA.summary: In a Fox interview on August 12, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the Federal Reserve to consider a 50-basis-point interest-rate cut at its September meeting, rather than the quarter-point cut broadly expected by markets. He argued that the latest employment data would have justified cuts in June and July and that a larger September reduction would allow the Fed to catch up.

USA.title: Trump threatens lawsuit over Fed headquarters construction costs
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to sue Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over alleged cost overruns in construction of the Fed headquarters. The threat added pressure on Powell amid debate over interest-rate cuts, but this intervention did not specify a monetary-policy demand or threaten removal or institutional changes.

USA.title: Bessent encourages Fed to cut rates by 1.5 to 1.75 percentage points
USA.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates by 1.5–1.75 percentage points and said he expected a 50-basis-point cut in September. His comments were discussed amid growing investor expectations of rate cuts. The linked reports do not establish a precise statement date, so the earliest publication date is used.

USA.title: Trump appoints Miran temporarily to the Fed
USA.summary: President Donald Trump's temporary appointment of Miran to the Federal Reserve was discussed as signaling his policy intentions and buying time before selecting Jerome Powell's successor. The discussion linked the appointment to growing influence for Trump-aligned views favoring aggressive interest-rate cuts and raised concerns about Fed independence, credibility and potential effects on the dollar.

USA.title: Pulte accuses Fed governor Cook of mortgage fraud
USA.summary: Federal Housing Finance Agency head Bill Pulte accused Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook of mortgage fraud in a social media post, alleging she designated two properties as primary residences on mortgage applications signed 14 days apart. He posted images of her signatures without the broader application context. Cook disputed the allegations and said she would defend herself; a Fed spokesperson initially declined comment. The post itself made no monetary-policy demand or explicit tenure threat.

USA.title: Trump demands Cook resign
USA.summary: President Donald Trump demanded on social media that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook “must resign now,” responding to mortgage-fraud allegations by Federal Housing Finance Agency head Bill Pulte concerning two properties allegedly designated as primary residences. Reports also said Trump was discussing firing Cook for cause if she refused. The allegations were not established by the reporting. Cook subsequently said she would not resign; a Fed spokesman initially had no immediate comment.

USA.title: Trump discusses firing Cook for cause
USA.summary: President Trump told aides he was considering firing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook for cause if she refused to resign, according to a senior White House official and another person familiar with the matter. The discussions followed mortgage-fraud allegations by Federal Housing Finance Agency head Bill Pulte. The report did not establish those allegations, and Trump's authority to fire Cook was described as contested. A Fed Board spokesman had no immediate comment.

USA.title: Bessent claims Fed rates are too high by all calculations
USA.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly asserted that Federal Reserve interest rates were too high according to all calculations, advocating lower rates. The report noted that he identified no supporting calculation and that no one else had found such a calculation.

USA.title: Bessent calls for a 50-basis-point September cut
USA.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in remarks quoted in the broadcast, urged the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates by 50 basis points in September. He argued that revised payroll figures would have prompted cuts in June or July had they been available then, and said rates were 150–175 basis points above where they should be.

USA.title: Trump accuses Powell of hurting housing
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump accused Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell of hurting the housing industry “very badly” in a Truth Social post reported during the week of August 21, 2025. The criticism targeted Powell’s refusal to cut interest rates; the linked report does not establish the post’s exact date.

USA.title: Trump calls for Lisa Cook to resign
USA.summary: President Donald Trump called for Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook to resign amid allegations by a Trump ally that she falsified housing-loan documents. Trump also called for a Justice Department investigation. Cook said she would not be bullied out of her job. The resignation demand did not specify a monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Justice Department urges Powell to remove Cook
USA.summary: The US Department of Justice wrote to Federal Reserve chair Jay Powell urging him to remove governor Lisa Cook amid allegations that she falsified housing-loan documents. The letter followed President Donald Trump's call for an investigation. Cook said she refused to be bullied out of her job.

USA.title: Trump ally accuses Cook of mortgage-document falsification
USA.summary: An unnamed Trump ally accused Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook of falsifying mortgage documents, allegedly listing two homes as primary residences to obtain lower mortgage rates. The allegations prompted subsequent pressure for her departure and a Justice Department investigation. Cook said she would not be bullied out of her job. The linked reports do not establish the allegations as fact.

USA.title: Trump calls for DOJ investigation of Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump called on the Justice Department to investigate Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook after a Trump ally accused her of falsifying housing-loan documents. The allegation was not established as fact in the report. The investigation demand came amid Trump's broader confrontation with the Fed; Cook said she would not be bullied out of her job.

USA.title: Justice Department decides to investigate Cook
USA.summary: The US Justice Department reportedly decided to investigate Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over allegations that she designated two purchased homes as primary residences to obtain lower mortgage rates. The report established neither wrongdoing nor a policy demand or removal threat by the department.

USA.title: Trump calls for Cook to resign
USA.summary: Donald Trump called for Federal Reserve policymaker Lisa Cook to resign during the week of August 22, 2025. A follow-up report noted that Cook faced allegations of irregularities in mortgage applications. The reports do not establish the exact date of Trump's demand or attach a specific monetary-policy direction to it.

USA.title: Trump announces firing of Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump announced that he was removing Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook, alleging that false statements on mortgage applications provided sufficient cause to fire her and questioning her trustworthiness. Cook disputed his legal authority, said no lawful cause existed and refused to resign, stating she would continue her duties. The Fed declined to comment. The attempted removal raised the prospect of a court battle over presidential authority to dismiss Fed governors.

USA.title: Trump threatens to fire Fed Chair Powell over steady rates
USA.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell over the Fed's decision to keep interest rates steady in 2025, pressuring the bank to lower rates. The August 26 report recalled the threat without establishing when it occurred.

USA.title: Pulte files mortgage-fraud complaint against Cook
USA.summary: Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte referred Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook to the Justice Department over alleged mortgage fraud. He alleged that she designated properties in two states as primary residences on 2021 mortgage applications, potentially obtaining better rates. The reports identify his complaint as triggering an investigation subsequently cited in President Trump's effort to remove Cook. Cook disputed the legality of her removal. The linked stories do not establish the complaint's exact date or report a monetary-policy demand by Pulte.

USA.title: Justice Department announces investigation of Cook
USA.summary: The US Department of Justice announced an investigation into Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook following a criminal complaint from Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte alleging possible mortgage fraud. The report framed the investigation as part of increased administration scrutiny of Democratic figures and pressure on the Fed. The allegations were not established findings, and the investigation announcement contained no specific monetary-policy demand.

USA.title: Trump announces removal of Fed governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump wrote to Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook announcing her removal for alleged false information on 2021 mortgage applications, asserting sufficient cause to dismiss her. Cook disputed his authority, refused to resign and planned a legal challenge; her lawyer said the attempted dismissal lacked factual or legal basis. The Fed said governors can be removed only for cause and that it would abide by any court decision. The move came amid Trump's broader calls for lower interest rates, but the removal announcement cited alleged misconduct rather than a policy demand.

USA.title: Pulte publicly accuses Cook of mortgage fraud
USA.summary: Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte publicly accused Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook on social media of submitting fraudulent information on two 2021 mortgage applications by listing properties in different states as her primary residences, potentially securing better mortgage terms. His post included images appearing to show her signature but, according to the reporting, no other evidence supporting the accusation. The accusation preceded a criminal referral and President Trump's removal announcement; the linked stories date the post only to the preceding week.

USA.title: Congressional Black Caucus condemns Cook's removal
USA.summary: The Congressional Black Caucus condemned President Trump's attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, calling it a racist, misogynistic and unlawful attack on the Fed's integrity and independence. Trump cited allegations concerning Cook's mortgage applications; Cook disputed grounds for removal and refused to resign. The caucus's statement advocated no monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Lutnick focuses Cook dispute on mortgage fraud
USA.summary: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told CNBC that the real question in the dispute over President Trump's attempted removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook was whether she committed mortgage fraud. His remarks questioned Cook's integrity without advocating a monetary-policy direction or explicitly demanding her removal. Cook disputed the grounds for dismissal and refused to resign; her lawyer said she would challenge the attempt in court.

USA.title: Justice Department opinion supports removal of regional Fed presidents
USA.summary: A Justice Department opinion stated that the Federal Reserve Board of Governors can fire regional Reserve Bank presidents at will, asserting broad removal authority affecting their institutional autonomy. The report cited the opinion as a potential route to replacing regional presidents with Trump-aligned officials, but reported no such removals or monetary policy demand. The opinion's issuance date was not specified.

USA.title: Trump announces attempted dismissal of Lisa Cook
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump announced in a public letter on Monday night that he was removing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook immediately, citing allegations that she designated two homes as primary residences when obtaining mortgages. Cook denied wrongdoing, disputed his authority to remove her and vowed to challenge the dismissal rather than resign. Her term runs until 2038; her removal could allow Trump to secure a majority of appointees on the seven-member Board. The Fed said it would abide by any court decision on Cook.

USA.title: Senator challenges Cook's qualifications at appointment
USA.summary: At the time of Lisa Cook's appointment to the Federal Reserve Board, an unnamed Republican senator alleged that she lacked monetary-policy expertise and instead held far-left views. The criticism challenged her qualifications without advocating a specific policy direction. The linked report does not establish the statement's exact date.

USA.title: Pulte accuses Cook of mortgage fraud
USA.summary: Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte, a Trump ally and prominent Federal Reserve critic, accused Fed governor Lisa Cook of mortgage fraud and submitted a criminal referral. The allegations concerned mortgage applications predating her Fed service and became the basis for Trump's attempt to remove her. The Justice Department was investigating, but no charges had been filed. Cook denied wrongdoing and said she would challenge her removal.

USA.title: Justice Department investigates Cook mortgage allegations
USA.summary: The US Justice Department took up mortgage-fraud allegations against Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook following a referral by Federal Housing Finance Agency director Bill Pulte. The allegations concerned mortgage applications predating her Fed service and were cited by President Trump in attempting to remove her. No investigative conclusion or formal criminal charges were reported. Cook denied wrongdoing. The department's investigation carried no reported monetary-policy demand.

USA.title: Trump announces immediate removal of Lisa Cook
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook was removed immediately, citing alleged false statements in mortgage documents and questioning her reliability as a financial regulator. Cook disputed the allegations and his authority to remove her, vowed to remain in office, and planned legal action. Her term runs until 2038, and no criminal charges were reported. The Fed said it would respect judicial decisions. Linked reports conflict on whether the announcement occurred on August 25 or August 26, 2025.

USA.title: Trump declares readiness for Cook legal fight and predicts Fed majority
USA.summary: President Donald Trump said he was ready for a legal fight over his attempt to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. He predicted his appointees would hold four of seven Board seats and highlighted their influence over regional Fed leadership, while calling for lower interest rates. Cook planned to challenge her removal in court; the Fed affirmed its independence and said it would respect judicial decisions.

USA.title: Trump urges quick nomination to replace Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump told advisers he wanted to announce a replacement quickly for Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, whose removal he was pursuing. Potential nominees included economic adviser Stephen Myron and former World Bank Group President David Malpass. Cook disputed Trump's authority to fire her and threatened legal action, while Trump prepared for a possible court fight.

USA.title: Trump publicly considers Myron for Cook's seat
USA.summary: President Trump told reporters he was considering his close economic adviser Stephen Myron to replace Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, whom he was trying to oust. Myron had already been nominated to another Board seat, but Cook’s carried a longer term. Cook disputed Trump’s authority to fire her and threatened legal action.

USA.title: Trump challenges Fed construction figures during building visit
USA.summary: President Donald Trump challenged Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over building-construction figures during a filmed site visit. The linked commentary describes conflicting figures and Powell attempting to explain them, characterizing Trump's treatment as humiliating. No monetary-policy demand or tenure or institutional threat is established for this encounter, and the stories do not establish its date.

USA.title: Trump announces Cook's dismissal in social media letter
USA.summary: In a social-media letter on August 25, President Donald Trump announced the dismissal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, asserting that allegations of mortgage fraud before her appointment constituted sufficient cause for removal. Cook had not been charged or convicted and disputed his authority, filing suit on August 28 to block the removal as unlawful. The Fed said it would abide by the courts’ decision. The intervention challenged the scope of governors’ statutory protection against removal without cause but contained no explicit monetary-policy demand.

USA.title: Housing agency chief refers Cook allegations to Justice Department
USA.summary: Bill Poulte, the Trump-appointed head of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, publicized mortgage-fraud allegations against Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook and referred them to the Justice Department. The allegations concerned conduct before her appointment and became Trump's stated basis for attempting to dismiss her. Cook had not been charged with a civil or criminal violation and pledged to challenge her removal in court.

USA.title: Trump declares intent to secure a Fed majority
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump declared, “We will obtain the majority,” referring to Federal Reserve leadership. The broadcast discussed his statement alongside potential Board vacancies, explaining that replacing Lisa Cook could increase the number of Trump-supporting governors from three to four on the seven-member Board. Commentators described the prospect as a concern for Fed independence; the quoted declaration itself specified no monetary-policy direction or statutory change.

USA.title: Trump claims low prices in renewed pressure for Fed cuts
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed in a social media post over the August 30–31, 2025 weekend that prices were down and inflation was virtually nonexistent, adding pressure on the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates. Reports linked his comments to investor concerns about Fed independence and increased demand for gold. The linked stories do not establish the exact posting date.

USA.title: Trump nominates White House adviser to Fed Board
USA.summary: President Donald Trump nominated White House economic adviser Stephen Myron to a vacant Federal Reserve Board seat, in what the reports described as an effort to increase White House influence over monetary policy and pursue rate cuts. At his September 4 Senate Banking Committee hearing, Myron, who shared Trump's support for lower rates, pledged to act independently based on his own economic analysis.

USA.title: Trump advocates greater influence over rates at cabinet meeting
USA.summary: At a cabinet meeting described in a September 4, 2025 report as occurring the previous week, President Trump advocated more direct influence over Federal Reserve interest-rate policy, including through confirmation of White House economic adviser Stephen Myron to the Board of Governors. The account does not establish a specific policy direction or the meeting's exact date.

USA.title: Justice Department opens criminal investigation into Cook
USA.summary: The US Justice Department opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over alleged false information on mortgage applications, issuing subpoenas concerning properties in Michigan and Atlanta. The probe followed two criminal referrals from housing director Bill Pulte. Cook denied committing mortgage fraud. The investigation came amid her lawsuit challenging President Trump's attempt to remove her from the Fed board; no monetary-policy demand was reported as part of the investigation.

USA.title: Pulte sends criminal referrals targeting Cook
USA.summary: Housing director Bill Pulte sent two criminal referrals to the Justice Department alleging that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook committed mortgage fraud involving multiple properties. The referrals led to a criminal investigation, including subpoenas and inquiries concerning properties in Michigan and Atlanta. Cook denied committing mortgage fraud, and her attorney rejected the allegations. The investigation occurred amid her legal challenge to President Trump's attempt to remove her.

USA.title: Trump threatens to fire Fed Chair Powell
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell. The threat was referenced in reporting on Stephen Myron's Senate confirmation hearing amid concerns about presidential influence over monetary policy and Federal Reserve independence. The report did not specify when Trump made the threat or identify a policy demand attached to it.

USA.title: Trump attempts to remove Fed Governor Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump attempted to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, alleging mortgage misrepresentations. Cook refused to resign and sued, arguing her dismissal was unlawful; the Justice Department also opened an investigation. Reports said replacing Cook alongside confirming Stephen Myron could create a board majority supportive of Trump's policies. A federal judge subsequently temporarily blocked her removal, finding she was likely to succeed in challenging its legality under the Federal Reserve Act.

USA.title: Trump challenges Fed renovation costs during site visit
USA.summary: During a visit to the Federal Reserve renovation site, President Donald Trump challenged Chair Jerome Powell over alleged cost overruns, claiming costs had increased from $2.7 billion to $3.1 billion. Powell disputed the calculation, saying it included a separate building completed five years earlier. Trump maintained that the building belonged to the overall work. The linked September 6 report replayed the exchange without establishing the visit's date.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Powell over delayed rate cuts on Truth Social
USA.summary: Following weaker jobs data, President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell on Truth Social, saying he should have lowered interest rates long ago and was, “as usual,” too late. The post followed a Senate confirmation hearing for Trump's Fed governor nominee Stephen Mirren by one day.

USA.title: Bessent calls for Fed policy recalibration
USA.summary: Scott Bessent called for the Federal Reserve to recalibrate policy ahead of its upcoming meeting. His call was reported amid debate over whether weakening employment data warranted an initial interest-rate cut of 50 rather than 25 basis points. The linked reports do not establish that he explicitly demanded a particular cut size or threatened Fed officials.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Fed organization and data sources
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump criticized the Federal Reserve's organization as broken and said it needed to use modern data sources. His remarks, reported the following day, challenged the Fed's functioning without advocating a specific monetary-policy direction or explicitly proposing institutional changes.

USA.title: Trump attempts to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump attempted to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over allegations that she misrepresented properties on mortgage applications. Cook denied the allegations and sued to retain her position. Reports cited documents casting doubt on the allegations. An appeals court ruling on September 15 allowed her to remain in office pending the dispute, including for the forthcoming policy meeting. The removal attempt raised concerns about Federal Reserve independence and political interference.

USA.title: Trump predicts a big Fed rate cut
USA.summary: Ahead of the Federal Reserve’s upcoming interest-rate decision, US President Donald Trump said he was expecting a “big cut,” reinforcing his pressure for lower rates. Reports contrasted his preference with market expectations of a quarter-percentage-point reduction. No threat or institutional action was established as part of this particular statement.

USA.title: Trump administration appeals ruling keeping Lisa Cook in office
USA.summary: The Trump administration appealed a court ruling keeping Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook in office despite President Trump's attempted removal. The September 15 broadcast reported that Cook remained on the Board and appeared likely to participate in the upcoming rate decision, with a ruling on the appeal expected that day or the next. No monetary-policy demand was identified in this intervention.

USA.title: Trump nominates White House adviser Stephen Myron to Fed Board
USA.summary: President Trump nominated White House Council of Economic Advisers chair Stephen Myron to a Federal Reserve Board seat running through year-end. Ahead of the September 15 Senate confirmation vote, Myron planned to take leave rather than resign from his White House role, drawing criticism over Fed independence and creating a reportedly unprecedented overlap in the modern Fed’s history. He said he would act independently and had not disclosed his intended policy vote. If confirmed, he was expected to participate in the policy meeting beginning the following day.

USA.title: Senate confirms Stephen Myron to Fed Board
USA.summary: The US Senate confirmed President Trump's nominee Stephen Myron to the Federal Reserve Board of Governors on September 15, enabling him to participate in the upcoming FOMC meeting. Reports described the confirmation as a win for Trump amid his pressure for lower interest rates. The confirmation itself established no specific policy demand, criticism, tenure threat or change to the Fed's institutional autonomy.

USA.title: Trump calls for three-percentage-point Fed rate cut
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called for the Federal Reserve to cut its base interest rate by three percentage points to lower mortgage, business and other borrowing costs, claiming this could save the government $1 trillion annually in debt interest. Economists cited in the coverage warned that such a large cut could instead raise inflation, long-term interest rates and government borrowing costs.

USA.title: Treasury secretary urges initial half-point Fed rate cut
USA.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Besson was reported as saying the Federal Reserve’s federal funds rate should be much lower and advocating an initial 50-basis-point reduction rather than a massive one-time cut. The report contrasted this approach with more aggressive rate-cut proposals.

USA.title: Trump attempts to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump attempted to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, accusing her of submitting fraudulent mortgage information. Cook's lawyers denied that she committed fraud, and she challenged the attempted dismissal in court. An appeals court rejected Trump's request for her immediate removal late on September 15, allowing her to remain ahead of the Fed's policy meeting. The linked reports do not date the original firing attempt or establish a policy demand specific to it.

USA.title: Trump demands immediate larger rate cut in Monday post
USA.summary: In a Monday morning social media post ahead of the Federal Reserve’s two-day policy meeting, President Donald Trump demanded that Chair Jerome Powell cut interest rates immediately and by more than he had planned. The report interpreted this as seeking a larger reduction than the widely expected quarter-percentage-point cut.

USA.title: Trump publicly calls for lower interest rates
USA.summary: In remarks excerpted in a September 16 report, President Donald Trump urged the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates, saying it was very important and describing the United States as the world's hottest country. The excerpt did not identify the occasion or establish a separate date for his remarks.

USA.title: Trump appoints Stephen Myron to Fed Board
USA.summary: The Trump administration selected Council of Economic Advisers chair Stephen Myron to fill the Federal Reserve Board vacancy left by Adriana Kugler. Accelerated Senate confirmation on September 15 enabled him to join the September rate-setting meeting, amid Trump's push for lower rates. Myron would take leave from, rather than resign, his White House job during the remaining term ending in January. Critics questioned whether this arrangement compromised the appearance of independence; Myron told senators he would act independently.

USA.title: Trump administration announces Supreme Court appeal over Cook removal
USA.summary: The Trump administration said it would appeal to the Supreme Court after a federal appeals court rejected its emergency request to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook ahead of the September policy meeting. Cook attended the meeting following the ruling.

USA.title: Trump orders Lisa Cook's dismissal
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump ordered Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook’s dismissal in August 2025, citing alleged mortgage irregularities that Cook denies. Cook challenged the dismissal in court, and a court blocked it, allowing her to remain in office and participate in the September policy meeting. The administration reportedly sought to take the case to the Supreme Court. The linked reports do not establish the dismissal order’s exact date or a policy demand attached to it.

USA.title: Trump calls for 300 basis points in rate cuts
USA.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump called for 300 basis points in Federal Reserve interest-rate cuts, urging substantially faster easing. Reports discussing the Fed’s September 17 quarter-point cut placed his demand that week but did not establish an exact day. Chair Jerome Powell defended the Fed’s pace, saying weakening job creation warranted easing after waiting to assess tariffs, inflation and employment.

USA.title: Trump sought a half-point Fed rate cut
USA.summary: Coverage reported that US President Donald Trump wanted the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates by half a percentage point rather than the quarter-point reduction delivered on September 17, its first cut of 2025. Fed Chair Jerome Powell justified the smaller cut as balancing rising employment risks against still-elevated inflation.

USA.title: Trump urges Fed to cut rates and listen to him
USA.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump urged the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates and listen to smart people like himself the day before its September 17 policy decision. The September 18 broadcast recounted his comments while discussing the Fed’s subsequent quarter-point rate cut and the challenges political pressure posed for communicating its policy independence.

USA.title: Warren calls Miran Trump's puppet before confirmation vote
USA.summary: Before Stephen Miran's Federal Reserve confirmation vote, Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren accused him of entering the bank as President Trump's puppet and a Trojan horse who would follow his master's instructions. Her criticism challenged his independence without advocating a specific monetary-policy direction. The linked report does not establish the statement's exact date; its publication date is used.

USA.title: Trump administration asks Supreme Court to allow Cook's removal
USA.summary: The Trump administration filed an emergency Supreme Court request to allow Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook’s removal while her lawsuit challenging her firing proceeds, after lower courts allowed her to remain. Solicitor General John Sauer argued that alleged misrepresentations on mortgage applications justified deeming her unfit to set interest rates. Cook denies mortgage fraud and has not been charged; she alleges the firing was a pretext to undermine Fed independence. Linked reporting also noted that mortgage documents reviewed by media outlets contradicted the administration’s allegations.

USA.title: Trump announces firing of Fed Governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump announced that he was firing Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, citing allegations that she supplied fraudulent mortgage application information before taking office to obtain favorable lending terms. He argued that the allegations made her unqualified and untrustworthy to serve. Cook denied mortgage fraud and challenged her removal in court, alleging that the justification was concocted to undermine Fed independence. Courts allowed her to remain while litigation proceeded; the administration subsequently sought Supreme Court intervention. The linked reports do not date the original announcement, so the earliest publication date is used.

USA.title: Trump publicly calls Powell terrible
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump publicly called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell “terrible,” according to a September 21, 2025 podcast recalling the earlier attack. The report does not establish the statement’s date or occasion, or attach a specific policy demand or threat to it.

USA.title: Trump confidant accuses Lisa Cook of false loan information
USA.summary: An unnamed Trump confidant accused Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook of providing false information in connection with a private loan. The September 21 report described the allegation as unsupported and said Trump used it as grounds to seek her dismissal. The confidant's accusation did not advocate a monetary-policy direction or explicitly demand Cook's removal.

USA.title: Trump says his side will have a Fed majority
USA.summary: President Donald Trump said his side would have a majority at the Federal Reserve, according to remarks quoted in a September 25 discussion. The discussion presented his statement as political pressure for lower interest rates and greater administration influence over the Fed. The quoted statement did not explicitly threaten removals or changes to the bank’s statutory independence.

USA.title: Trump announces intention to fire Lisa Cook
USA.summary: In late August 2025, US President Donald Trump announced his intention to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. Coverage linked the attempted removal to mortgage-related allegations and reported that many analysts viewed it as an effort to gain control of the Fed. On October 1, the Supreme Court deferred a decision, allowing Cook to remain in office for now. The linked stories do not establish the exact announcement date or a policy demand specific to this intervention.

USA.title: Trump seeks removal of Fed Governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump sought the removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, an effort ongoing around Stephen Miran’s first policy meeting in September 2025. An October 11 discussion reported that Cook remained in office under a court ruling, with further proceedings expected in January, and highlighted potential implications for Fed independence. The stories do not establish a specific date or policy demand for this removal effort.

USA.title: Bessent criticizes central bank balance-sheet expansion
USA.summary: In recent articles discussed by the Financial Times on October 9, 2025, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized the extent of central-bank balance-sheet expansion, bringing renewed scrutiny to the Federal Reserve’s quantitative easing. He characterized the expansion as mission creep and compared QE to a lab experiment. The report did not establish the articles’ publication dates or identify any accompanying tenure or institutional threat.

USA.title: Trump appoints Miran to the Federal Reserve
USA.summary: President Donald Trump's appointment of Stephen Miran to the Federal Reserve was described by commentators as placing a 'Trojan horse' inside the bank amid efforts to steer monetary policy and pressure Chair Jerome Powell. The account did not establish a specific policy demand or change to the Fed's statutory autonomy through this appointment.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell late on everything
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell an “anti-person” and said he was late on everything on October 28, 2025, the day before the Fed’s policy decision. The remarks criticized Powell’s judgment amid Trump’s repeated pressure for lower interest rates.

USA.title: Trump appoints Stephen Miran to the Fed
USA.summary: President Donald Trump's appointment of Stephen Miran to the Federal Reserve was discussed in a November 11, 2025 broadcast as a concrete intervention, contrasting with his earlier rhetoric about the Fed. Speakers characterized the appointment as a risk to institutional independence and linked it to expectations of a more dovish Fed. These were commentators' assessments; the story does not establish the appointment date or an explicit policy demand by Trump associated with the appointment.

USA.title: Trump attempts to remove Lisa Cook from Fed
USA.summary: President Trump attempted to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook amid allegations concerning her mortgage applications. Cook’s lawyer argued that apparent discrepancies were accurate when made or inadvertent and did not constitute fraud given other disclosures. The Supreme Court temporarily blocked the removal pending arguments in January.

USA.title: Trump demands lower rates and voices wish to fire Powell at investment forum
USA.summary: At a U.S.–Saudi investment forum in Washington, President Donald Trump said Federal Reserve interest rates were too high and voiced a desire to fire Chair Jerome Powell, saying Treasury Secretary Scott Bessant had advised against it. Trump also publicly told Bessant to fix the rate issue quickly or be fired, a remark described in one report as a joke. The comments came amid divisions among Fed policymakers over a December rate cut.

USA.title: Trump reiterates wish to remove Powell in Oval Office remarks
USA.summary: Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office about selecting the next Federal Reserve chair, President Donald Trump said he believed he knew whom he would choose. He reiterated that he would remove Chair Jerome Powell if he could, but said others were preventing him from doing so. Powell’s term as chair was due to end in May 2026, while his term as a Fed governor extended to 2028.

USA.title: Hassett says Fed has lost control of inflation
USA.summary: White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett said the Federal Reserve had lost control of inflation. His remarks were reported amid US inflation remaining above 3% and uncertainty over tariffs’ inflationary effects. The linked report establishes no specific policy demand or threat accompanying his criticism.

USA.title: Trump places Stephen Miran on Fed Board
USA.summary: President Donald Trump placed Stephen Miran on the Federal Reserve Board. Commentary published on November 24, 2025, cited the appointment as evidence of increased politicisation of the Fed and a potential source of pressure for lower interest rates. The stories do not establish the appointment date or a specific policy demand, criticism or threat made by Trump in this intervention.

USA.title: Hassett calls for December rate cut using growth figures
USA.summary: White House official Kevin Hassett, described as working closely with President Trump, argued that the Federal Reserve should cut interest rates in December, citing figures indicating negative quarter-over-quarter US growth. A November 26 podcast recalled the intervention without specifying its date. Commentator Karl-Arne alleged that Hassett had invented the figures or used statistics unavailable to others at the time.

USA.title: Trump berates Powell over Fed building renovations
USA.summary: President Donald Trump berated and belittled Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell in a dispute over the central bank's building renovations, according to a Bloomberg HT commentator recalling the confrontation on November 26, 2025. The commentator discussed it as pressure on Powell amid Trump's preference for lower interest rates, but did not establish a specific rate demand or threat during that confrontation or identify its date.

USA.title: Bessent contrasts Fed renovations with personally funded office work
USA.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized the Federal Reserve’s building renovation spending by contrasting it with renovations to his own office, which he said he was paying for personally. The November 26 report recalled his remarks without establishing when they occurred; it attributed no monetary-policy demand or institutional threat to this intervention.

USA.title: Bessent calls for a simpler, less prominent Federal Reserve
USA.summary: Scott Bessent, the US Treasury secretary, criticized the Federal Reserve's activities and balance sheet as overly complicated, called for it to take a less prominent role, and said he was seeking a chair accordingly. Bloomberg HT commentators discussed possible greater Treasury prominence and interpreted simplification as potentially limiting Fed holdings to Treasury securities; neither was reported as an explicit Bessent demand.

USA.title: Trump says next Fed chair will favor rate cuts
USA.summary: President Donald Trump said he had decided whom to nominate as Federal Reserve chair and that his appointee would, like him, be more inclined toward interest-rate cuts. The report identified Kevin Hassett as the leading prospective nominee, but did not establish that Trump had named him.

USA.title: Trump attempts to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump attempted to remove Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook over mortgage-related allegations. The December 8 reports recalled the attempt ahead of an anticipated hearing, without establishing its date or reporting a new ruling. They highlighted questions about legal protections for Fed officials and the implications for central-bank independence if the removal were upheld.

USA.title: Hassett says he would cut interest rates as Fed chair
USA.summary: Kevin Hassett, described as the leading candidate to become Federal Reserve chair and an adviser to presidents, said he would cut interest rates if he were chair. Reports also attributed to him a call for six-month forward guidance. His remarks were reported as occurring at the end of the week before December 8, without an exact date, ahead of a Fed meeting at which markets widely expected a rate cut.

USA.title: Bessent and Hassett advocate changes to regional Fed leadership
USA.summary: A December 8 report attributed to Bessent and Hassett proposals to change the Federal Reserve's regional leadership arrangements. They argued that regional Fed presidents speak too frequently and should be required to have lived in their regions for three years. The report presented these as structural changes to the Fed, without attributing a monetary-policy direction to this intervention.

USA.title: Hassett urges Fed to provide six-month policy guidance
USA.summary: Kevin Hassett, described as a presidential adviser and the expected next Federal Reserve chair, urged the Fed ahead of its forthcoming announcement to provide public guidance on its interest-rate or economic outlook over the next six months. He said failing to do so would be irresponsible. Commentators disputed the criticism, noting that the Fed already provides verbal guidance and numerical projections.

USA.title: Hassett urges larger rate cuts at WSJ CEO Council summit
USA.summary: Speaking at the WSJ CEO Council summit on December 9, White House National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett said there was ample room to lower Federal Reserve interest rates, subject to the data, agreeing that this meant more than a quarter percentage point. Hassett, reported as a leading contender for Fed chair, also expressed concern that the Fed had been partisan. Asked about political loyalty if appointed, he said he would follow his own judgment and committed to nonpartisanship. His remarks came as divided Fed policymakers met ahead of an expected quarter-point cut.

USA.title: Trump makes immediate rate cuts a test for Fed chair selection
USA.summary: In an interview with Politico, US President Donald Trump answered yes when asked whether cutting interest rates immediately was a litmus test for choosing the next Federal Reserve chair. He thereby made immediate monetary easing a selection criterion, ahead of Jerome Powell's scheduled departure from the chairmanship in May 2026.

USA.title: Trump attempts to remove a Fed governor
USA.summary: President Donald Trump attempted to remove an unnamed Federal Reserve governor. A December 10 report described the effort as unsuccessful so far but provided neither the grounds for removal nor a policy demand tied to the attempt.

USA.title: Trump scrutinizes Fed renovation during site inspection
USA.summary: During a joint inspection of the Federal Reserve’s building renovation, President Donald Trump confronted Fed Chair Jerome Powell over project costs. A Bloomberg HT commentator discussing the visit on December 10, 2025, characterized Trump’s treatment of Powell as an effort to discredit him and speculated that the pressure could contribute to another rate cut. The account does not establish a monetary-policy demand during the visit or the visit’s exact date.

USA.title: Hassett favors a larger cut at upcoming Fed meeting
USA.summary: Kevin Hassett, discussed as a possible successor to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, said he would cut interest rates by more than 25 basis points at the upcoming Fed meeting if the decision were his. The linked coverage described his preference as a possible 50-basis-point cut and front-loading of easing. No threat or institutional change accompanied this demand.

USA.title: Trump criticizes latest Fed cut as insufficient
USA.summary: At a White House event on December 10, President Donald Trump criticized the Federal Reserve’s quarter-point rate cut as too small, saying it should have been at least twice as large. He disparaged Chair Jerome Powell and argued that excessive concern about inflation was restraining growth. The Fed cut rates to 3.5–3.75%, while Powell said it was well positioned to wait and assess economic developments.

USA.title: White House floats district residency requirement for Fed governors
USA.summary: The White House administration was reported to be discussing a requirement that prospective Federal Reserve governors live within a particular district for three years before appointment. Speaking on Bloomberg, strategist Mark Cranfield characterized the suggestion as part of efforts to alter the Fed’s balance of power, while questioning whether it would gain traction. No specific monetary-policy demand accompanied the reported proposal.

USA.title: Trump calls December rate decision a test for Powell
USA.summary: Ahead of the Federal Reserve’s December 2025 rate decision, US President Donald Trump called the decision another test for Chair Jerome Powell, amid his pressure for faster interest-rate cuts. The linked report does not establish the statement’s exact date. The Fed subsequently cut rates by 25 basis points to 3.5–3.75%.

USA.title: Trump urges much lower rates while discussing chair candidates
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump, discussing meetings with finalists to succeed Jerome Powell as Federal Reserve chair, said he was not asking candidates to commit to interest-rate cuts but stated that rates should be much lower. His remarks advocated easier policy without an explicit threat or commitment requirement.

USA.title: Trump calls Fed deadhead and demands double the rate cut
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called the Federal Reserve a “deadhead Fed” after its latest 25-basis-point interest-rate cut and demanded a reduction at least twice as large. Fed Chair Jerome Powell said the bank would pause to assess the effects of three cuts that year and identified Trump's tariffs as the primary reason inflation remained above target.

USA.title: Trump demands much lower rates and a presidential voice
USA.summary: In a Friday statement discussing Federal Reserve chair candidates Kevin Hassett and Kevin Warsh, President Donald Trump praised both and said US interest rates should be far below their current level. He also asserted his right as president to comment on interest rates. In a subsequent CBS interview, Hassett said the president’s views should be considered but emphasized that the Fed makes decisions independently.

USA.title: Hassett says Fed should consider Trump's rate views
USA.summary: In a weekend CBS interview reported on December 15, 2025, Kevin Hassett, a presidential adviser and prospective Federal Reserve chair, said President Donald Trump's statements and views on the interest-rate path were important and should be considered. Hassett also emphasized that the Fed makes its decisions independently. The report does not establish the interview's exact date.

USA.title: Republican senators criticize Fed interest payments on reserves
USA.summary: Unnamed Republican senators criticized the Federal Reserve’s interest payments on banks’ reserves as a waste of Fed and, by extension, US government money, arguing that they reward banks for doing nothing and should end. The criticism was reported in an FT News Briefing discussion of JPMorgan’s shift from Fed deposits into US Treasuries; no specific date for the senators’ statements was provided.

USA.title: Trump says next Fed chair will favor much lower rates
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump said his forthcoming choice for Federal Reserve chair would be someone who believed interest rates should be lower by "a lot." The statement signaled a preference for substantial monetary easing in selecting the next chair, without an explicit removal threat or proposal to change the Fed's mandate or autonomy.

USA.title: Hassett voices support for Fed independence
USA.summary: Kevin Hassett, discussed as a candidate for Federal Reserve chair, said he supported the Fed’s independence. The December 18 report placed his statement in the previous week without specifying a day, citing it in a discussion of how Trump’s eventual appointee might balance presidential preferences with market confidence. No policy demand, criticism or threat was attributed to Hassett in this intervention.

USA.title: Trump urges rate cuts despite strong GDP data
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump urged the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates despite stronger-than-expected US GDP growth of 4.3%, arguing that the positive figures should not prevent easing. His remarks were reported in a December 24 discussion of overnight US economic news.

USA.title: Trump attempts to dismiss Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump attempted to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook in 2025. The attempted removal was under legal challenge, with Supreme Court arguments expected early in 2026. The linked report does not establish the precise date or a policy demand specific to this intervention.

USA.title: Federal prosecutors open criminal investigation into Powell
USA.summary: US federal prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell concerning headquarters renovation spending and his Senate testimony. The Fed received grand jury subpoenas on January 9 threatening criminal charges. Announcing the action on January 11, Powell denied wrongdoing and alleged that the investigation was a pretext for political intimidation over interest-rate decisions. He pledged to continue serving. The investigation specified no monetary-policy demand or removal action; Trump denied involvement.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Powell in NBC phone call
USA.summary: In a telephone call with NBC, President Trump denied involvement in the criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell concerning headquarters renovations, but criticized Powell's job performance and knowledge of building construction. Powell said the investigation was a consequence of the Fed's recent decisions. Trump expressed no policy demand or tenure threat in this intervention.

USA.title: Tillis threatens to block Fed confirmations during investigation
USA.summary: Republican Senator Tom Tillis said he would not confirm any Federal Reserve appointee while the investigation involving Chair Jerome Powell and headquarters renovations remained ongoing. His pledge followed grand jury subpoenas that Powell described as a pretext for pressure on the Fed's independence. Tillis advocated no monetary policy direction or change to the Fed's mandate.

USA.title: Trump threatens renovation lawsuit against Powell
USA.summary: In December 2025, President Donald Trump threatened a lawsuit against Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, alleging incompetence over cost overruns in the renovation of two historic Fed buildings. The report does not establish the exact date or identify a monetary-policy demand, removal threat or proposed institutional change associated with this intervention.

USA.title: Trump seeks to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump sought to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. The linked reports describe her case as heading before the Supreme Court, with potential implications for presidential authority to remove Federal Reserve board members. They do not establish a monetary-policy demand or specify when the removal effort began.

USA.title: Trump raises possible legal action against Powell in August
USA.summary: In August 2025, US President Donald Trump said he was considering allowing legal action against Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the Fed’s building renovation project. The report recalls this as an earlier legal threat preceding the January 2026 criminal investigation. It does not establish the exact August date or a specific monetary-policy demand accompanying that statement.

USA.title: Trump presses for lower rates during Fed construction visit
USA.summary: During a visit to the Federal Reserve’s renovation site alongside Chair Jerome Powell, President Donald Trump jokingly insisted that he was more concerned about lowering interest rates than about the project’s cost overruns. Trump also cited a renovation budget figure that Powell corrected downward. The linked account recalls the visit without establishing its exact date.

USA.title: Truman removes Eccles as Federal Reserve chair
USA.summary: President Harry Truman removed Marriner Eccles as Federal Reserve chair in 1948, according to the story’s historical discussion of chairs remaining as governors. Eccles stayed on the Board of Governors rather than resigning. The account establishes neither an exact date nor a policy demand associated with his removal.

USA.title: Authorities pursue renovation-related allegations against Powell
USA.summary: US federal prosecutors opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell concerning his congressional testimony about renovations to the Fed’s Washington headquarters, including whether he misrepresented the project’s scope. The investigation involved a Justice Department subpoena and threats of criminal charges. In a video released on January 11, Powell called the allegations a pretext for pressure on the Fed’s independent interest-rate decisions and pledged to continue his Senate-confirmed duties. Trump said he knew nothing about the subpoena and denied that the investigation concerned interest-rate disagreements.

USA.title: Republican senator threatens to withhold support for next Fed chair
USA.summary: Republican Senator Tillis of North Carolina criticized the criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, alleging that the legal system was being used for other purposes. He pledged to withhold support for any new Fed nominee, including Powell's successor as chair, until the investigation was resolved, potentially complicating confirmation of President Trump's nominees.

USA.title: Trump attempts to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump attempted to remove Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook. A January 12, 2026 discussion recalled the attempt and said the dispute was due to be considered in court that month, placing it in the context of efforts to change the Fed's membership and policy orientation. It did not establish the removal attempt's date or a specific policy demand attached to it.

USA.title: Hassett defends Powell investigation as accountability
USA.summary: Kevin Hassett, a top White House economic adviser and finalist to succeed Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, defended the Justice Department’s criminal investigation into Powell as promoting accountability. His remarks came amid criticism that the investigation threatened Fed independence. Hassett’s statement included no monetary-policy demand or explicit threat to Powell’s tenure.

USA.title: Trump denies rate dispute motivated Powell investigation
USA.summary: In an NBC News interview, President Donald Trump said he knew nothing about the Justice Department's subpoena concerning Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell and denied that the criminal investigation was related to White House disagreements with Powell over interest rates. The investigation concerned the Fed's headquarters renovation. Trump made no explicit policy demand or threat in this statement.

USA.title: Trump accuses Powell of renovation cost overruns during Fed visit
USA.summary: During a televised visit to the Federal Reserve renovation site in July 2025, President Donald Trump accused Fed Chair Jerome Powell of cost overruns, citing spending of $3.1 billion. Powell examined Trump's document and disputed the accusation, saying the total included costs for another building renovated five years earlier. The linked report does not establish the visit's exact date.

USA.title: Criminal investigation targets Powell over Fed renovations
USA.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell disclosed on Sunday evening that the US Justice Department was investigating the Fed’s headquarters renovations, including cost overruns and whether Congress had been accurately informed, and had issued subpoenas. Powell rejected the allegations and described the threat of criminal charges as pressure over the Fed’s independent interest-rate decisions. Reports portrayed the investigation as intimidation of Powell and other rate-setters. Trump denied knowing about the investigation; Powell indicated he would continue serving his term.

USA.title: Trump calls for one-percent interest rates
USA.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump said U.S. interest rates should be at 1 percent, pressing the Federal Reserve for substantially lower rates. A January 12, 2026 report quoted the statement without identifying its occasion or original date.

USA.title: Tillis vows to block Fed nominations over investigation
USA.summary: Republican Senator Tom Tillis said in a Sunday-night statement that he would block all Trump administration Federal Reserve nominations until the legal cloud surrounding the investigation into the Fed was cleared. His position on the Senate Banking Committee could prevent nominees, including a successor to Chair Jerome Powell, from advancing to a Senate vote. He made no monetary-policy demand.

USA.title: Justice Department subpoenas Fed with criminal prosecution threat
USA.summary: The US Justice Department served the Federal Reserve with subpoenas threatening criminal charges concerning Chair Jerome Powell’s June congressional testimony about headquarters renovations. Disclosing the action on January 11, Powell called the renovation allegations a pretext for pressure over the Fed’s refusal to follow presidential interest-rate preferences and pledged to continue his duties. The reported action contained no explicit monetary-policy demand or removal threat.

USA.title: Trump attempts to remove Fed governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump attempted to remove Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook. The January 13, 2026 report recalled the attempt as background to disputes over Fed independence and said the resulting case would reach the Supreme Court later that month. It did not establish the date of the attempted removal or identify a policy demand specific to it.

USA.title: Pulte suggests renovation testimony could justify Powell's removal
USA.summary: Trump ally Bill Pulte suggested that allegations Jerome Powell had lied under oath about Federal Reserve building renovations could provide legal grounds to remove him as Fed chair. The allegations concerned Powell’s congressional testimony disputing claims of extravagant project features; the story did not establish that he had lied. Pulte’s reported intervention advocated no monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Luna formally requests Justice Department investigation of Powell
USA.summary: Representative Anna Paulina Luna formally asked the Justice Department to investigate Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell amid allegations that he had lied under oath to Congress about the Fed’s building renovation project. Powell had disputed claims that the project included extravagant amenities. The report does not date Luna’s request or attribute a monetary-policy demand or removal threat to her.

USA.title: Tillis vows to block Trump Fed nominees during Powell investigation
USA.summary: Republican Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina, a Senate Banking Committee member, said he would not approve any new Trump nominee to the Federal Reserve while the investigation into Fed Chair Jerome Powell remained ongoing. His pledge threatened to obstruct confirmations in the closely divided committee. Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski reportedly supported his position. Tillis did not advocate a monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Murkowski supports Tillis's opposition to nominations
USA.summary: Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski of Alaska supported Senator Thom Tillis's refusal to approve new Trump nominees while the investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell continued. Murkowski also criticized the subpoenas targeting Powell. Her intervention opposed the investigation and supported a nomination blockade without advocating a particular interest-rate policy.

USA.title: Justice Department subpoenas Powell
USA.summary: The US Justice Department subpoenaed Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, threatening criminal consequences apparently concerning his congressional testimony about Fed building renovations. The subpoena itself was not available in the reporting. Powell alleged that the action stemmed from the Fed's refusal to set monetary policy according to President Trump's wishes, rather than genuine concerns about renovations. Trump denied knowing about the subpoenas. The reports establish no explicit policy demand by the Justice Department or demand for Powell's removal.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Powell in NBC interview
USA.summary: In a Sunday-night NBC News interview, President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell as "not very good at the Fed" and "not very good at building buildings." Trump denied knowing about subpoenas received by the Fed concerning its headquarters renovations. His remarks attacked Powell's competence but included no explicit policy demand or threat.

USA.title: Scott challenges Powell over renovation features
USA.summary: At Jerome Powell’s regular Senate Banking Committee update in mid-2025, Republican Senator Tim Scott challenged the Federal Reserve’s renovation plans, citing rooftop garden terraces, ornate water features, elevators serving a VIP dining suite and white marble. Powell called some descriptions misleading, saying the elevator already existed and some features were no longer planned. The linked report does not establish the hearing’s exact date.

USA.title: Trump disputes renovation costs during Fed site visit
USA.summary: During a July 2025 visit to the Federal Reserve’s renovation site with Chair Jerome Powell, President Donald Trump challenged the project's cost, claiming it had risen from $2.7 billion to $3.1 billion. Powell disputed the figure, saying he had not heard it from anyone at the Fed and that Trump had included a third building. Asked afterward whether the overruns were grounds for dismissal, Trump downplayed the issue, saying overruns happen and he wanted to help finish the project. The linked reports do not establish the visit’s exact date.

USA.title: Trump attempts to dismiss Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump attempted to dismiss Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook in August 2025. Cook challenged her removal in federal court, and courts allowed her to remain in office during the litigation. The reports also describe a subsequent Justice Department investigation into alleged mortgage fraud, which Cook denied. As of January 13, 2026, the Supreme Court was expected to hear her case the following week. The stories do not establish the exact dismissal date or a policy demand specific to this intervention.

USA.title: Tillis criticizes Powell subpoenas
USA.summary: Republican Senator Thom Tillis, a member of the Senate Banking Committee, criticized the subpoenas targeting Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over his testimony about headquarters renovations. In a Sunday-night statement, Tillis called the action a “vindictive prosecution” and said he would oppose all Fed nominees, including the next chair, until the matter was resolved. His opposition could prevent nominees from receiving committee approval.

USA.title: US Justice Department opens Powell investigation
USA.summary: The US Justice Department opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell concerning alleged waste, concealed renovation costs and his congressional testimony about the Fed’s headquarters project. Its opening date is not established; Powell disclosed it in a video on January 11, 2026. US Attorney Jeanine Pirro said the Fed had ignored repeated inquiries. Powell called the investigation a pretext for political pressure on monetary policy and pledged to continue serving. No indictment was reported, and President Trump denied ordering the investigation.

USA.title: Republican senators question Powell on renovation
USA.summary: During Jerome Powell’s June 2025 testimony before the Senate Banking Committee, Republican senators challenged the Federal Reserve chair about headquarters renovation costs and reported project features. Powell disputed some descriptions as misleading and said certain features were no longer planned. The Fed attributed some cost overruns to unforeseen conditions, including asbestos and soil contamination. The story does not establish the hearing’s exact date.

USA.title: White House budget director challenges Powell testimony
USA.summary: Following Jerome Powell’s June Senate testimony, White House budget director Russell Vogt sent the Federal Reserve chair a letter challenging his account of the Fed headquarters renovation. The letter said his testimony conflicted with public building plans, implying that Powell either misled Congress or that the Fed failed to notify relevant building authorities of changes. Powell defended his testimony. The story does not establish the letter’s exact date.

USA.title: Trump blames Powell for expensive housing
USA.summary: In a public remark replayed in the linked report, President Donald Trump blamed Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for keeping interest rates too high, saying people could not buy houses and calling Powell a “numscull.” The remark pressed for lower rates and attacked Powell’s judgment. The report does not establish the date of the original statement.

USA.title: Justice Department investigates Lisa Cook
USA.summary: The U.S. Justice Department opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over alleged mortgage fraud after President Trump announced her removal in August 2025. Cook denied wrongdoing, and courts allowed her to remain in office while she challenged her removal. The report does not establish the investigation's exact opening date or identify a monetary-policy demand attached to it.

USA.title: Pirro defends Powell investigation on X
USA.summary: In a Monday-night post on X, US Attorney Janine Pirro defended the Justice Department investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over the Fed’s headquarters renovations. She alleged that her office had contacted the Fed about the renovations multiple times but had been ignored. Her post did not advocate an interest-rate policy or demand Powell’s removal.

USA.title: Murkowski backs blocking Fed chair nominations
USA.summary: Republican Senator Lisa Murkowski backed Senator Thom Tillis’s call to block nominations for Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s successor amid the Justice Department investigation into Powell. Calling the investigation “nothing more than an attempt at coercion,” she opposed the investigation without advocating a particular monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell incompetent or crooked
USA.summary: Answering reporters’ questions before a trip to Michigan for an economic speech, President Donald Trump said Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell was either “incompetent” or “crooked” and did not do a very good job. His remarks concerned the criminal investigation into Powell over the Fed headquarters renovation and his congressional testimony. Trump made no specific policy demand or removal threat in this statement.

USA.title: Justice Department subpoenas Federal Reserve
USA.summary: The US Justice Department subpoenaed the Federal Reserve in a criminal investigation involving Chair Jerome Powell, concerning the Fed headquarters renovation and alleged false statements to Congress. News became public over the weekend before January 13, 2026; the stories do not establish the subpoenas' issuance date. In a Sunday evening video, Powell alleged that the investigation reflected political pressure over monetary policy rather than legitimate oversight. The Fed had published documents and clarifications about the renovation. The investigation prompted public defenses of Powell and central-bank independence.

USA.title: Republican senator threatens to block Powell successor
USA.summary: An unnamed Republican senator said he would reject any Trump nominee to succeed Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell until the criminal legal matter involving Powell was resolved. The pledge was reported amid opposition to the investigation and ahead of the end of Powell’s chairmanship in May; it advocated no monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Justice Department subpoena escalates pressure on Powell
USA.summary: Federal prosecutors sent grand jury subpoenas to the Federal Reserve concerning Chair Jerome Powell’s testimony last summer about the bank’s building renovation project. The reports described this as an escalation beyond President Trump’s earlier unsuccessful removal efforts and reputational attacks. In a Sunday message, Powell alleged that the legal pressure reflected the administration’s displeasure with his refusal to lower interest rates as Trump wanted. Former Fed chairs, other central-bank leaders and JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon warned against the pressure and its implications for central-bank independence.

USA.title: Trump attacks Powell over market reactions to good news
USA.summary: In remarks reported the following day, US President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, saying good economic news should lift markets rather than depress them through expectations that the Fed would not take the needed interest-rate steps.
