Advocating easier policy, Trump called Powell a “jerk” and said that, fortunately, Powell would leave and things would then normalize. These remarks did not specify a removal action or institutional change.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell incompetent or corrupt before Detroit trip
USA.summary: Speaking as he left the White House before flying to Detroit, U.S. President Donald Trump accused Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell of doing a poor job and alleged that budget overruns on renovations to Federal Reserve buildings showed Powell was either incompetent or corrupt. This intervention did not include an explicit policy demand or threat to Powell’s tenure or the Fed’s autonomy.

USA.title: Trump conditions Fed chair selection on commitment to cut rates
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump said he would not select a new Federal Reserve chair unless the candidate committed to lowering interest rates. The January 14, 2026 report recalled this condition without dating the statement and raised concerns about its implications for central-bank independence.

USA.title: Justice Department investigates Fed Chair Powell
USA.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell disclosed on Sunday evening that he faced a US Department of Justice criminal investigation and subpoenas. Powell alleged that the action was pressure to lower interest rates, rather than a matter concerning his congressional testimony or Fed building costs, and said he would continue doing his job independently. Wall Street executives and central bankers expressed concern about threats to Fed independence, while the market reaction was muted.

USA.title: Trump says he has no plans to dismiss Powell
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump said he currently had no plans to dismiss Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, stepping back from renewed discussion of removing him before May. The statement contained no explicit policy demand or renewed dismissal threat.

USA.title: Justice Department subpoenas Fed over Powell testimony
USA.summary: The US Justice Department subpoenaed the Federal Reserve in a criminal investigation into whether Chair Jerome Powell made false statements to a Senate committee about headquarters renovation costs. Disclosing the proceedings on January 11, 2026, Powell called them a pretext to pressure the Fed into lowering interest rates. Trump denied being behind the investigation. The reports describe an ongoing investigation, not an indictment, and do not establish the subpoena's issuance date.

USA.title: Trump challenges Powell on renovation costs during site visit
USA.summary: During a joint visit to the Federal Reserve headquarters construction site in July 2025, US President Donald Trump publicly challenged Chair Jerome Powell over renovation costs, claiming they had risen above $3 billion and handing him a supporting document. Powell disputed the figure, explaining that it included a separate building completed five years earlier, not the current renovation project. The linked accounts do not establish the exact day or report a monetary-policy demand or tenure threat during this exchange.

USA.title: Trump signals preference to keep Hassett outside Fed
USA.summary: At a White House health care event, President Trump told National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett that he wanted to keep him in his current role, praising his television appearances and contrasting them with Federal Reserve officials, particularly Chair Jerome Powell, whom he said did not talk much. The remarks signalled that Hassett might no longer be Trump's preferred successor to Powell, whose chairmanship term ends in May. Trump made no monetary policy demand in this intervention.

USA.title: Trump calls Powell corrupt and incompetent
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell a “jerk,” corrupt and incompetent during the week covered by the January 17, 2026 report. The remarks came amid a criminal investigation into whether Powell had lied about Federal Reserve renovation costs. Trump denied being behind the investigation. The report does not establish the exact day of these remarks or attach a specific policy demand to them.

USA.title: Trump insults Powell over refusal to lower rates
USA.summary: In an archival recording replayed in a January 17, 2026 podcast and described as roughly six months old, US President Donald Trump criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for refusing to lower interest rates. Trump called Powell unintelligent and stupid, suggested Powell hated him, and said neither insults nor his nickname “Too Late” had changed Powell’s behavior. The recording’s exact date was not established.

USA.title: Trump attacks Lisa Cook over alleged mortgage fraud
USA.summary: In August 2025, President Donald Trump attacked Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook over alleged mortgage fraud in an effort to remove her. The report identifies federal housing finance chief Bill Pulte as behind the attack and discusses it in the context of expanding Trump's influence over Fed appointments. It reports that a Supreme Court hearing concerning Cook was scheduled for January 21, 2026. The linked account does not establish the exact date of the August intervention or substantiate the fraud allegation.

USA.title: Trump advocates lower rates when markets perform well
USA.summary: In a speech during the week reported on January 17, 2026, US President Donald Trump advocated lower Federal Reserve interest rates, saying, “When the market is doing great, interest rates can go down,” and calling this the “old-fashioned way of economics.” The linked report does not establish the speech’s exact date.

USA.title: Trump seeks dismissal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump attempted to dismiss Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook in August 2025 through a letter posted on Truth Social, citing mortgage-fraud allegations that she denies. The linked reports do not establish the exact dismissal date. Cook challenged her removal, and lower courts blocked it while litigation continued. At Supreme Court arguments on January 21, 2026, justices questioned the administration’s position, including the process afforded Cook and the implications for Fed independence. Fed Chair Jerome Powell attended the hearing.

USA.title: Criminal investigation opened against Fed chair
USA.summary: The US Justice Department opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell concerning the renovation of the Fed’s Washington headquarters and his statements about it. Linked reports portrayed the probe as an escalation of President Donald Trump’s pressure for lower interest rates and an effort to establish grounds for Powell’s removal. Powell said the threat of criminal charges reflected the Fed’s refusal to follow the president’s rate preferences and defended evidence-based monetary policy. The stories do not establish the investigation’s opening date.

USA.title: Powell denounces criminal investigation as pressure to cut rates
USA.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell disclosed a Justice Department investigation and alleged that threatened criminal charges were a pretext to remove him and pressure the Fed to lower interest rates in line with President Donald Trump's wishes. The investigation concerned his statements about renovations to Fed buildings. Powell defended monetary decisions based on evidence and economic conditions rather than political intimidation. The linked reports give conflicting dates for his disclosure.

USA.title: Bessant criticizes Powell's attendance at Cook hearing
USA.summary: Speaking to CNBC in Davos, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessant criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's attendance at the Supreme Court hearing on President Trump's attempted removal of Governor Lisa Cook. He called it inappropriate and a mistake, accusing Powell of politicizing the Fed and trying to influence the court. Bessant questioned supporting Cook without a Fed examination of mortgage-fraud allegations, which she denies, and criticized Powell for not meeting federal prosecutors before grand jury subpoenas concerning the Fed's building project.

USA.title: Warren and Durbin demand records on Fed criminal probe
USA.summary: Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren and Dick Durbin demanded records from the Trump administration concerning the criminal investigation into the Federal Reserve’s building project, calling the probe a serious misuse of power. Their intervention challenged the investigation without advocating a monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Trump attempts to dismiss Fed governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump attempted to dismiss Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook. A January 26, 2026 discussion recalled that Cook remained in office and said Supreme Court justices appeared unimpressed by the attempted removal. The story does not establish the attempt's date or a policy demand attached to it.

USA.title: Trump advocates weaker dollar in 2019 tweet
USA.summary: In a 2019 tweet during his first presidential term, Donald Trump said that an overly strong dollar was hurting manufacturers and growth. The linked retrospective presents this statement as explaining his pressure on the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates, weaken the dollar and support American exports. The exact date of the tweet is not established.

USA.title: Trump calls for Powell's removal and arrest over renovations
USA.summary: In a recorded statement replayed in the story, US President Donald Trump said he wanted to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell, called him enormously incompetent and demanded his arrest over allegedly spending $4 billion on a small building. The remarks targeted the Fed’s building renovations rather than advocating a monetary-policy change. The recording’s original date was not provided.

USA.title: Trump attacks Powell and demands loyalty in Davos speech
USA.summary: In a Davos speech the week before January 26, 2026, US President Donald Trump called Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell a terrible chair and mocked him as “Too Late,” criticizing his timing on interest-rate cuts. Trump alleged that Powell had favored the opposing political side before the election. The report described Trump as demanding presidential loyalty from the Fed chair and portraying failure to follow presidential instructions as disloyalty.

USA.title: Trump accuses Fed of killing every rally
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump accused the Federal Reserve of killing “every rally,” amid his repeated demands for substantial interest-rate cuts and public attacks on Chair Jerome Powell. The remarks were reported ahead of a Fed rate decision and a possible announcement of Powell’s successor. Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel described Trump’s attacks as deeply concerning and warned against undermining Fed independence.

USA.title: Federal Reserve served with grand jury subpoenas
USA.summary: The Federal Reserve was served with grand jury subpoenas amid the Trump administration's threatened criminal prosecution of Chair Jerome Powell. Linked reports associated the pressure with demands for lower interest rates; Powell rejected the threatened indictments as an attempt to influence rate decisions. The reports did not specify the subpoenas' subject or demands. At his subsequent January 28 press conference, Powell avoided political questions and defended Fed independence.

USA.title: Bessant criticizes Powell for attending Cook hearing
USA.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessant criticized Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell for attending Supreme Court oral arguments on whether the president can fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook. The report gives no date for Bessant's criticism. Powell defended his attendance, calling the case potentially the most important in the Fed's history and noting that previous Fed chairs had attended Supreme Court cases.

USA.title: Trump administration brings charges against Powell
USA.summary: Trump's administration reportedly pursued legal action against Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell amid presidential pressure for lower interest rates. One report described charges without specifying them; another identified Justice Department grand-jury subpoenas concerning Powell's 2025 congressional testimony about Fed headquarters renovations. Powell largely declined to discuss the investigation at his January 28 press conference and stressed the Fed's independence as it held rates at 3.5–3.75%.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Fed in reaction to rate decision
USA.summary: In a clip presented as his reaction to the Federal Reserve’s rate decision, President Donald Trump criticized Fed leadership and complained that its response to positive economic figures depresses markets. He advocated a looser policy approach, arguing that US growth potential could be much higher. The clip’s transcript is partly garbled and establishes no specific threat against Fed officials or its institutional autonomy.

USA.title: Trump launches criminal investigation into Powell
USA.summary: Reports attributed to President Donald Trump a Justice Department criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell concerning renovations to the Fed’s building. Powell denied wrongdoing. Lawmakers from both parties raised concerns about interference with Fed independence, and Republican Senator Thom Tillis pledged to block Fed confirmations until the probe was resolved. The investigation was reported amid Trump’s separate demands for lower interest rates and selection of Powell’s successor.

USA.title: Trump calls for US interest rates of 1%
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump called for interest rates of 1%, advocating substantially looser Federal Reserve policy. Both reports cited this demand while discussing the selection of Kevin Warsh as the next Fed chair, but neither specified when Trump made the statement.

USA.title: Tillis threatens to block nominees over Fed investigation
USA.summary: Republican Senator Tom Tillis of North Carolina reiterated that he would block Federal Reserve nominees until the Justice Department's investigation into the Fed and Chair Jerome Powell was resolved or dropped. Speaking after President Trump's announcement of Kevin Warsh as his chosen successor to Powell, Tillis called Warsh qualified but maintained his opposition, describing the Powell and Lisa Cook cases as attempts to undermine Fed independence. His stance posed an obstacle to Warsh's confirmation. The Powell investigation concerned Fed building renovations; Powell denied wrongdoing.

USA.title: Trump nominates Kevin Warsh to lead the Federal Reserve
USA.summary: President Donald Trump announced on social media that he had nominated former Federal Reserve governor Kevin Warsh to succeed Jerome Powell as Fed chair, subject to Senate confirmation. Trump praised Warsh’s economics and research experience, emphasized their longstanding acquaintance and predicted he could become the Fed’s best chair. The announcement contained no explicit policy demand, criticism of the Fed or threat.

USA.title: Trump selects Kevin Warsh to succeed Powell
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump selected former Federal Reserve governor Kevin Warsh to succeed Jerome Powell when Powell's chairmanship expires in May, subject to Senate confirmation. The selection came amid Trump's stated desire for a chair more responsive to his calls for lower interest rates, after the Fed held rates steady on January 28. Reports noted Warsh's recent support for faster rate cuts alongside his historically hawkish views, leaving uncertainty about how closely he would follow Trump's preferences.

USA.title: Investigation into Fed building renovations
USA.summary: The US Justice Department opened an investigation involving Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over costly renovations to the Fed's building. Powell characterized the inquiry as pressure connected to President Donald Trump's efforts to secure lower interest rates, rather than an innocuous investigation. The reports do not establish misconduct or a policy demand by investigators. The probe also reportedly complicated Senate confirmation prospects for Powell's nominated successor, Kevin Warsh.

USA.title: Senators threaten to block Fed nominees over Powell case
USA.summary: Some US senators reportedly said they would not approve any Trump nominees while the legal case against Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell remained in place. The threatened confirmation blockade was described as a possible obstacle to Kevin Warsh's confirmation as Fed chair. The report did not identify the senators and questioned whether they would maintain their position following Warsh's nomination.

USA.title: Bessant article criticizes expansion of Fed power
USA.summary: In an article published in 2025, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessant argued that the Federal Reserve had undergone 'gain of function,' becoming too powerful, and advocated challenging its expanded role. The linked report associates his criticism with quantitative easing, which Fed officials defended as part of the normal central-bank toolkit. The article's exact publication date is not established.

USA.title: Tillis reiterates condition for approving Fed nominee
USA.summary: In a Friday interview, Republican Senator Thom Tillis reiterated that he would block Federal Reserve appointments, including Kevin Warsh's nomination as chair, until the investigation involving Jerome Powell ended. The investigation concerned Powell's congressional testimony about Fed building renovations. Tillis's pivotal position on the Senate Banking Committee made his condition an obstacle to Warsh's confirmation; he did not advocate a monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Fed nominees who change course after appointment
USA.summary: Speaking in Davos, US President Donald Trump criticized prospective Federal Reserve appointees who say pleasing things before appointment but act differently once in office. He said he had previously been disappointed by this discrepancy. The linked account does not establish the day of the remarks or report a specific policy demand or threat in this intervention.

USA.title: Justice Department subpoenas Powell over renovation testimony
USA.summary: The Department of Justice sent subpoenas to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell in an investigation into his 2025 congressional testimony about renovations to the central bank’s building. The report does not specify when the subpoenas were sent or establish a policy demand, tenure threat or proposed institutional change associated with them.

USA.title: Trump calls for Powell investigation to continue
USA.summary: Speaking to reporters at the White House, President Donald Trump said the Justice Department investigation involving Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell should continue to its conclusion. The investigation concerned Powell’s 2025 congressional testimony about renovations to Federal Reserve buildings. Trump’s statement did not advocate a monetary-policy direction or explicitly threaten Powell’s tenure or the Fed’s institutional autonomy.

USA.title: Trump calls for Fed leadership favoring cuts when markets rise
USA.summary: In a quoted statement about his preferred Federal Reserve leadership, U.S. President Donald Trump said he wanted someone who would allow interest rates to fall when markets were doing well. He argued that a stronger country should mean lower, not higher, interest rates. The linked report presented the remarks as presidential pressure on the Fed for monetary easing.

USA.title: Trump says he would not nominate a Fed chair who would raise rates
USA.summary: Donald Trump said he did not expect his Federal Reserve chair nominee to raise interest rates and would not have nominated him if he expected increases. His remarks made avoiding rate increases a stated condition of his selection.

USA.title: Trump challenges next Fed chair to deliver 15% growth
USA.summary: In a Fox interview on Monday, President Donald Trump said the next Federal Reserve chair should be able to raise US economic growth to 15%, setting a growth expectation without specifying a monetary-policy action. Discussing the statement, economist Nathan Sheets questioned whether the United States could achieve growth anywhere near that rate.

USA.title: Justice Department subpoenas Powell over renovation testimony
USA.summary: The U.S. Justice Department sent subpoenas to Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell in an investigation into his 2025 congressional testimony about renovations to the central bank’s building. The linked report does not establish the subpoenas’ date, a policy demand or a threat to Powell’s tenure or the Fed’s autonomy.

USA.title: Thom Tillis vows to block Fed nominees pending Powell investigation resolution
USA.summary: Republican Senator Thom Tillis of North Carolina, a pivotal member of the committee handling Federal Reserve nominations, said he would not vote for any Fed nominees until the Justice Department investigation into Jerome Powell was resolved. The investigation concerns Powell’s 2025 congressional testimony about renovations to the Fed’s headquarters. Tillis’s position poses an obstacle to Kevin Warsh’s confirmation as Fed chair.

USA.title: Justice Department subpoenas Fed in Powell investigation
USA.summary: U.S. Attorney Janine Piro opened a criminal investigation into whether Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell gave false congressional testimony about Fed building renovations, and the Justice Department issued two subpoenas to the Fed. On March 13, a federal judge struck down the subpoenas as improper, finding that their purpose was to harass and pressure Powell to yield to the president or resign. Piro said she would appeal. Powell subsequently said he would remain on the Fed board until the investigation was fully resolved.

USA.title: Piro announces appeal of ruling striking down Fed subpoenas
USA.summary: U.S. Attorney Janine Piro said she would appeal a federal judge’s ruling striking down two Justice Department subpoenas to the Federal Reserve. The subpoenas concerned her criminal investigation into whether Fed Chair Jerome Powell gave false congressional testimony the previous summer. The judge characterized their purpose as harassing and pressuring Powell to yield to the president or resign; no specific monetary-policy demand by Piro was reported.

USA.title: Trump places Stephen Myron on Fed to pursue rate cuts
USA.summary: The report describes President Donald Trump as having appointed Stephen Myron to the Federal Reserve's policymaking body specifically to pursue interest-rate cuts. It links that assignment to Myron's support for an immediate quarter-point cut at the March 18 meeting, when the Fed instead maintained its rate range at 3.50–3.75%. The appointment date is not specified.

USA.title: Trump gives incoming Fed chair Kevin Warsh a rate-cut mandate
USA.summary: A March 19 report described incoming Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh as carrying a mandate from President Donald Trump to lower interest rates, the same objective it attributed to Stephen Myron's appointment. The report followed the Fed's decision to hold rates at 3.50–3.75 percent. It predicted that Warsh would face Trump's anger if he did not pursue cuts, but identified no explicit threat or institutional change.

USA.title: Trump renews Powell dismissal threat in Fox Business interview
USA.summary: In a Fox Business interview aired April 15, President Donald Trump threatened to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell if he did not leave on time, saying he had previously held back from dismissing him. Trump also defended continuing the criminal investigation concerning the Fed’s renovation project. Powell had said he would not leave the Fed’s board while the investigation remained ongoing. The standoff complicated the confirmation of Trump’s nominated successor, Kevin Warsh.

USA.title: Prosecutors visit Fed construction project amid Powell probe
USA.summary: Two Justice Department prosecutors made an unannounced visit to the Federal Reserve's building renovation project as part of an ongoing criminal investigation into Chair Jerome Powell over alleged project mismanagement. They were turned away for safety reasons. The investigation continued despite a federal judge blocking subpoenas of Powell concerning the project; the visit involved no reported monetary-policy demand or tenure threat.

USA.title: Tillis conditions Fed confirmations on ending Powell investigation
USA.summary: Retiring Republican Senator Tom Tillis has repeatedly said he will not confirm any Federal Reserve nominee until the criminal investigation into Chair Jerome Powell ends. His position creates an obstacle to Kevin Warsh’s confirmation as Fed chair, while President Trump continues to support the investigation. The linked report does not date Tillis’s statements more precisely.

USA.title: Tillis pledges to block Warsh nomination pending DOJ probe resolution
USA.summary: Republican Senator Tom Tillis of North Carolina pledged to block Kevin Warsh’s nomination as Federal Reserve chair until the Justice Department’s investigation of Jerome Powell was resolved or dropped. Tillis argued that the probe undermined Fed independence; later coverage also described his demand as covering investigations of other Fed officials, including Lisa Cook. His objection concerned the investigations rather than Warsh’s suitability, and threatened to stall the nomination in the Senate Banking Committee.

USA.title: Warsh prepared testimony calls for review of Fed models and communication
USA.summary: In prepared testimony excerpts reported by Bloomberg ahead of his Senate Banking Committee appearance, Federal Reserve chair nominee Kevin Warsh questioned the suitability of the Fed’s economic models for today’s world and called for reviewing its models and communication. At the subsequent hearing, he also advocated a broader data foundation for measuring price changes. He emphasized that the Fed should remain independent of the US government, without advocating a specific interest-rate direction in this intervention.

USA.title: Warren challenges Warsh to demonstrate independence from Trump
USA.summary: During Kevin Warsh’s Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing for Federal Reserve chair, Senator Elizabeth Warren challenged his credibility on independence from President Trump. Citing his earlier claim that he was a “tough guy” who could stand up to Trump, she demanded that he name an aspect of Trump’s economic agenda he disagreed with. Warsh responded that the Fed should stay within its remit rather than identifying a disagreement.

USA.title: Warsh urges Fed to stay within its remit at confirmation hearing
USA.summary: At his Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing, Federal Reserve chair nominee Kevin Warsh told Senator Elizabeth Warren that the Fed had wandered outside its remit into other areas and should stay in its lane if he were confirmed. His criticism did not specify a monetary-policy direction or propose changes to the Fed’s statutory mandate or autonomy.

USA.title: Trump attempts to fire Fed governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump attempted to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. Senators raised the attempt as a concern about Fed independence during Kevin Warsh’s April 21, 2026 confirmation hearing for Fed chair. Warsh said he was not a legal expert and wanted the legal issues to play out in court. The linked reports do not establish when Trump attempted the removal or a policy demand specific to that intervention.

USA.title: Administration pursues criminal probe into Powell
USA.summary: The Trump administration maintained a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's congressional testimony about cost overruns on Fed building renovations. Powell alleged that the investigation was a pretext to pressure the Fed over interest rates. The probe blocked Kevin Warsh's confirmation because Republican Senator Thom Tillis refused to advance Fed nominees until it ended. On April 24, the Justice Department announced its closure in favor of an inspector-general review, while reserving the possibility of reopening it if warranted.

USA.title: Warsh calls for a new inflation framework at Senate hearing
USA.summary: At his Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing, Donald Trump's nominee for Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, blamed the Fed for allowing inflation to surge after the pandemic. Saying high prices remained a problem, he called for a regime change in monetary policy and a new inflation framework, without specifying its design or an interest-rate direction. He also said he would act independently of Trump if confirmed.

USA.title: Trump suggests Warsh would follow his lower-rate agenda
USA.summary: President Donald Trump suggested that Kevin Warsh, if confirmed as Federal Reserve chair, would follow his agenda, including lowering interest rates, which Trump argued was necessary. The report discussed the suggestion in connection with Warsh's confirmation hearing, where Warsh denied that he would be the president's "sock puppet."

USA.title: Warren challenges Warsh over Fed independence at confirmation hearing
USA.summary: During Kevin Warsh’s Federal Reserve chair confirmation hearing, US Senator Elizabeth Warren questioned his independence, warning that a presidential “sock puppet” could let Donald Trump use the Fed’s powers to enrich himself, his family and Wall Street allies. Asked whether he would be Trump’s sock puppet, Warsh replied, “Absolutely not.”

USA.title: Trump insists Powell investigation should continue in CNBC interview
USA.summary: In a CNBC interview a few days before April 24, 2026, President Trump insisted that the Justice Department continue investigating Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over testimony about Fed building renovation costs. Trump questioned why work he claimed should cost $25 million was costing billions. Powell said the investigation was pressure over interest rates. The Justice Department subsequently ended the probe; the exact interview date is not established.

USA.title: Trump threatens to fire Powell
USA.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell; the report did not specify the threat's timing, terms or associated policy demand. It reported the threat alongside a criminal investigation into Powell's congressional testimony about Fed renovation costs, which Powell said was intended to pressure the Fed over interest rates. The Justice Department announced on April 24 that it was ending that investigation.

USA.title: Pirro publicly pledges to continue Powell case
USA.summary: US attorney Jeanine Pirro publicly pledged to continue the criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's congressional testimony about cost overruns on renovations of two Fed buildings. The statement came days before the Justice Department announced the investigation's closure on April 24, 2026. The report does not establish the statement's exact date or identify a policy demand or threat to Powell's tenure or the Fed's mandate.

USA.title: Pirro closes Powell probe while reserving right to restart it
USA.summary: US Attorney Jeanine Pirro announced that she was closing the criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell’s congressional testimony about Fed renovation costs, leaving an existing Fed inspector-general review to proceed. She nevertheless said she would not hesitate to restart a criminal investigation if the facts warranted it. Powell denied wrongdoing and described the probe as pressure over interest rates. Its closure eased an obstacle to Kevin Warsh’s confirmation as Fed chair; a Fed spokeswoman declined to comment.

USA.title: Tillis blocks Fed nominees until Powell probe ends
USA.summary: Republican Senator Tom Tillis opposed confirming any Federal Reserve nominee until the criminal investigation into chair Jerome Powell ended, reiterating his objections at Kevin Warsh’s confirmation hearing. Tillis viewed the probe into renovation costs and Powell’s congressional testimony as an attack on Fed independence. His blocking vote impeded Warsh’s nomination. After prosecutors closed the investigation on April 24, Tillis lifted his opposition on April 26, following reported assurances about conditions for reopening it.

USA.title: Trump says rates will fall when Warsh takes office
USA.summary: President Donald Trump said interest rates would fall when his Federal Reserve chair nominee, Kevin Warsh, took office. Senator Elizabeth Warren quoted the statement at Warsh’s confirmation hearing, saying Trump had made it the previous week, and argued that it showed he expected Warsh to deliver his preferred rates rather than act independently. Warsh denied having agreed with Trump to lower rates and said he would act independently if confirmed. The statement’s exact date is not established.

USA.title: Warren challenges Warsh on independence and financial conflicts
USA.summary: At Kevin Warsh’s Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing, Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren called the Federal Reserve chair nominee Trump’s puppet and challenged his independence by asking whether Trump lost the 2020 election. She demanded details on disclosure and disposal of confidential assets, raising potential conflicts involving his employer Stanley Druckenmiller and investments in Trump businesses. Warsh maintained that he would act independently, denied making an interest-rate agreement with Trump, and said he had agreed with the Office of Government Ethics to sell the relevant assets.

USA.title: Warsh advocates a smaller Fed balance sheet at confirmation hearing
USA.summary: At his Senate confirmation hearing, Federal Reserve chair nominee Kevin Warsh advocated shrinking the Fed’s enlarged balance sheet. He also argued that AI-driven productivity gains could allow interest-rate cuts without increasing inflation and described inflation as a choice. Warsh denied agreeing with President Trump to cut rates or follow his instructions, asserting that he would act independently if confirmed.

USA.title: Tillis lifts block on Warsh confirmation
USA.summary: US Republican Senator Tom Tillis said he would lift his block on Kevin Warsh’s nomination as Federal Reserve chair after prosecutors closed their criminal investigation into Jerome Powell. Speaking on Meet the Press, Tillis said he supported confirmation after obtaining Justice Department assurances intended to protect Fed independence. His remarks indicated that the investigation would reopen only if the Fed’s inspector general recommended it. Tillis had withheld support over concerns that the investigation undermined the central bank’s independence.

USA.title: Justice Department investigates Powell over Fed renovation
USA.summary: The US Justice Department investigated whether Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell misled Congress about a $2.5 billion headquarters renovation with roughly $700 million in cost overruns. Announced in January 2026, the probe was denied by Powell, who characterized it as administration pressure to lower borrowing costs. The linked reports establish no policy demand by prosecutors. The investigation ended on April 24, reportedly finding no evidence of criminal wrongdoing, clearing an obstacle to Kevin Warsh’s confirmation as Powell’s successor.

USA.title: Trump attempts to dismiss Fed governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump attempted to dismiss Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook over allegations of mortgage fraud, which she denied. Cook remained at the Fed. The April 27, 2026 report described the attempted removal as a challenge to Fed independence but did not establish its date or an associated monetary-policy demand.

USA.title: Bessent says Fed need not rush rate cuts
USA.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in recent press remarks that, given current conditions, the Federal Reserve need not hurry to lower interest rates. His comments supported delaying cuts amid energy-price and inflation concerns associated with the war in Iran. The linked April 27 report did not establish the date of his remarks or report any accompanying criticism or threat.

USA.title: Justice Department moves to withdraw Powell subpoenas
USA.summary: The US Justice Department announced it was closing its criminal investigation into Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell and withdrawing subpoenas concerning his congressional testimony about headquarters renovation costs. The matter was referred to the Fed's inspector general. The announcement helped secure Senator Tom Tillis's support for Kevin Warsh's nomination as Fed chair. Powell welcomed the closure but subsequently said he would remain a governor until the investigation was definitively over.

USA.title: Tillis blocks Warsh pending end to Fed investigations
USA.summary: Republican Senator Tom Tillis of North Carolina said he would block Kevin Warsh’s nomination to lead the Federal Reserve from advancing through the Senate Banking Committee until the Trump administration dropped investigations into Fed officials Lisa Cook and Jerome Powell. The reports recall this earlier, undated condition while describing his subsequent decision to support confirmation after receiving Justice Department assurances. His condition did not advocate a monetary-policy direction.

USA.title: White House backs continued inspector general scrutiny of Fed renovation
USA.summary: At a White House briefing, the spokesperson backed continued Federal Reserve inspector general scrutiny of alleged financial misconduct in the Fed’s renovation, citing cost overruns and alleged taxpayer losses as a presidential priority. The spokesperson said the inspector general had substantial investigative resources and urged swift Senate confirmation of Kevin Warsh as Fed chair. Asked whether President Trump might fire Jerome Powell if he remained a governor, the spokesperson said they had not discussed that specifically and expected Trump to be satisfied once Warsh became chair.

USA.title: Pirro threatens to restart Powell investigation
USA.summary: US Attorney Jeanine Pirro said over the weekend that she would not hesitate to reopen the criminal investigation concerning Federal Reserve building-project cost overruns, after announcing its closure on April 24. The Justice Department subsequently said reopening would require a criminal referral from the Fed’s inspector general. Fed Chair Jerome Powell responded that he would remain a governor until the investigation was fully resolved with transparency and finality, and expressed concern about legal actions affecting Fed independence.

USA.title: Trump launches investigation into Powell over Fed renovation
USA.summary: The Trump administration's Justice Department opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over alleged mischaracterizations in congressional testimony about headquarters renovation cost overruns. Reports on April 30, 2026 said the probe had been dropped the previous week and referred to the Fed's inspector general. Powell warned that the administration's legal attacks threatened Fed independence and said he would remain a governor until the investigation was fully over. The reports do not establish when the investigation began.

USA.title: Trump ridicules Powell's decision to remain a governor
USA.summary: President Donald Trump ridiculed Jerome Powell’s decision to remain on the Federal Reserve Board after leaving the chairmanship, claiming he was staying only because he could not find another job and nobody wanted him. Powell had said he would keep a low profile as a governor. Trump’s remarks contained no monetary-policy demand or explicit threat to Powell’s tenure.

USA.title: Justice Department limits grounds for reopening Fed investigation
USA.summary: In a weekend statement recalled by Jerome Powell at his final press conference as Federal Reserve chair, the Justice Department said it would not reopen its investigation without a criminal referral from the Fed’s inspector general. Without that referral, it would not use its appeal to restart the investigation or issue new subpoenas. Powell welcomed the developments but reiterated that he would remain on the Board until the investigation was conclusively and transparently resolved. The statement’s exact date is not established.

USA.title: Justice Department closes Fed renovation investigation
USA.summary: The US Justice Department closed a criminal investigation concerning renovation of the Federal Reserve’s headquarters, clearing an obstacle to Senate confirmation of President Trump’s nominee Kevin Warsh as the next Fed chair. The report did not specify when the investigation was closed or establish any policy demand or threat associated with its closure.

USA.title: Trump administration rules out a central bank digital dollar
USA.summary: The Trump administration ruled out a Federal Reserve-issued digital dollar, favoring privately issued digital money through stablecoins instead. Bloomberg reported the decision during a discussion of Europe's digital euro project, noting that the GENIUS Act provided a regulatory framework for the private-sector approach. The story did not specify when the administration made the decision.

USA.title: Senate confirms Warsh as Federal Reserve chair
USA.summary: The U.S. Senate confirmed Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve chair by 54–45, with Democrat John Fetterman joining Republicans. The confirmation came amid concerns about Fed independence and President Trump's calls for sharply lower interest rates. Warsh said he would preserve monetary independence and had made no policy promises to Trump. The confirmation itself established no policy demand or threat to Fed autonomy.

USA.title: Van Hollen questions Warsh's independence on Senate floor
USA.summary: Speaking on the Senate floor during consideration of Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve chair, Senator Chris Van Hollen questioned whether Warsh's shift toward sharply lower interest rates reflected genuine economic judgment or President Trump's preferences. He said the alignment raised a legitimate question about Warsh's independence but did not automatically disqualify him. Warsh said he would preserve monetary independence and had made no policy promises to Trump.

USA.title: Nixon urges Burns to push for lower rates
USA.summary: In a recorded exchange during his reelection campaign, President Richard Nixon pressed Federal Reserve Chair Arthur Burns to push for lower interest rates. After Burns mentioned an upcoming Federal Open Market Committee meeting, Nixon urged him to “kick him in the rum a little.” The linked retrospective reports that Burns subsequently yielded to pressure and lowered rates, but does not establish the exchange’s exact date.

USA.title: Trump criticizes Powell during Fed headquarters visit
USA.summary: During a visit to Federal Reserve headquarters described as occurring the previous summer, President Donald Trump publicly accused Fed Chair Jerome Powell of going over budget on an office renovation. Asked before television cameras what Powell could say to make him back off his criticism, Trump replied that he would love Powell to lower interest rates. The linked report does not establish the visit's exact date.

USA.title: Justice Department opens criminal probe into Powell
USA.summary: The U.S. Justice Department opened a criminal investigation into Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell over his handling of headquarters renovations and their costs. Powell denied wrongdoing and publicly characterized the probe as part of presidential pressure to force lower interest rates. A White House spokeswoman said Trump had not directed the investigation. Lawmakers from both parties challenged the probe, which was subsequently dropped, although later reports described continuing uncertainty about its final resolution. The linked stories do not establish the investigation's opening date.

USA.title: Trump attempts to fire Fed governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: In August 2025, President Donald Trump attempted to fire Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook over unproven mortgage-fraud allegations. The reporting says Cook was not given a meaningful opportunity to respond. She sued, challenging the president’s authority and grounds for removing her, and remained in office as the case reached the Supreme Court. The linked stories do not establish the exact day of the attempted removal.

USA.title: Trump discusses firing Powell in December 2018
USA.summary: In December 2018, President Donald Trump discussed firing Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell amid a market sell-off, opposing the Fed’s four interest-rate increases that year. The retrospective report notes that Fed governors can be removed only for cause, not simply over disagreements about interest rates. The exact day of Trump’s dismissal discussions is not established.

USA.title: Trump threatens to fire Powell in 2025
USA.summary: After returning to office in 2025, US President Donald Trump threatened to fire Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell amid pressure for lower interest rates. The retrospective reports describe this direct threat as preceding Trump's attempted removal of Governor Lisa Cook and the Justice Department's investigation into Powell, but do not establish its exact date.

USA.title: Trump nominates Walsh to lead the Fed and lower rates
USA.summary: President Donald Trump nominated Kevin Walsh to chair the Federal Reserve with the explicit expectation that he would lower interest rates; one report described willingness to cut rates as a prerequisite for appointment. The Senate confirmed Walsh as Jerome Powell’s successor, although the stories do not establish the nomination date. Reports noted that Walsh’s earlier policy positions did not align with Trump’s preference for easier policy. Walsh told senators he would defend Fed independence and was not Trump’s puppet.

USA.title: Warren challenges Walsh's independence at confirmation hearing
USA.summary: At Kevin Walsh’s Senate Banking Committee confirmation hearing, Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren challenged his independence as prospective Federal Reserve chair, asking whether Donald Trump lost the 2020 election and whether Walsh disagreed with Trump on anything. Walsh referred to Congress’s certification of the election and offered a non-policy disagreement about Trump’s description of him. Warren’s questioning challenged his ability to act independently of the president without advocating a particular monetary policy.

USA.title: Warren calls Walsh Trump's puppet
USA.summary: Democratic Senator Elizabeth Warren described incoming Federal Reserve chair Kevin Walsh as President Donald Trump's puppet, questioning his independence from the president. The May 17 podcast recalled this characterization without dating the original statement or attributing a specific monetary-policy demand to Warren.

USA.title: Trump calls Fed leadership moronic for not lowering rates
USA.summary: In a recorded statement replayed in coverage of Jerome Powell's departure as Federal Reserve chair, US President Donald Trump said, "We have a moron at the Fed," and questioned why interest rates were not being lowered. The remarks attacked Powell's judgment and pressed the Fed to cut rates. Neither linked story establishes when Trump originally made the statement.

USA.title: Trump questions whether Powell is America's bigger enemy
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump questioned whether Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell or China's Xi Jinping was America's bigger enemy. The retrospective account links the attack to Trump's opposition to Fed interest-rate increases during a strong economy early in Powell's tenure, but does not establish the statement's exact date.

USA.title: Justice Department opens investigation into Powell over renovations
USA.summary: The US Justice Department opened an investigation alleging that Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell mishandled renovations to the bank’s headquarters. In a January 2026 video response, Powell characterized the threat of criminal charges as retaliation for setting interest rates on economic evidence rather than presidential preferences. Republican Senator Tom Tillis subsequently said he would block a Senate floor vote on Powell’s proposed successor unless the probe was dropped. The linked report does not establish the investigation’s opening date.

USA.title: Tillis threatens to block Fed chair nomination over Powell probe
USA.summary: Republican Senator Tom Tillis of North Carolina said he would block Trump's nominee to succeed Federal Reserve Chair Jay Powell from advancing to a Senate floor vote unless the criminal investigation into Powell was dropped. His intervention followed Powell's January video address alleging that the investigation was pressure over the Fed's interest-rate decisions. The story does not establish the exact date of Tillis's statement.

USA.title: Trump urges Warsh not to restrain strong growth
USA.summary: At Kevin Warsh’s White House swearing-in as Federal Reserve chair, President Donald Trump said Warsh should be totally independent and disregard political influence, but then urged him not to restrain a booming economy, arguing that strong growth does not cause inflation. Trump said, “We want to stop inflation, but we don’t want to stop greatness.” His remarks came amid rising inflation and investor expectations that the Fed’s next move could be a rate increase rather than his preferred cut.

USA.title: Bessent urges inflation-framework debate after return to 2%
USA.summary: Scott Bessent advocated discussing what inflation measures and how it should be interpreted, but said the discussion should wait until inflation returned to 2%. A May 30, 2026 podcast recalled his statement as having occurred the previous year, without giving an exact date. The intervention concerned the Federal Reserve’s inflation framework but established no specific demand for easing, tightening or institutional change.

USA.title: Hassett urges Fed to look past oil supply shock
USA.summary: In an interview following strong US jobs figures, White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett urged the Federal Reserve to look past an oil-driven supply shock, advocating a less restrictive response to energy-related inflation. The linked report does not attribute an explicit rate-cut demand, criticism of Fed competence or institutional threat to Hassett.

USA.title: Trump urges rate cuts to ease defense spending costs
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump urged the Federal Reserve chair to cut interest rates amid renewed fighting involving Iran and Israel. He argued that lower financing costs would give him room to increase defense spending, saying he could not afford that spending at current costs.

USA.title: Trump makes rate cuts a condition for Fed chair selection
USA.summary: President Donald Trump said he would not select a Federal Reserve chair who would not cut interest rates, making support for monetary easing a condition of selection. The statement was recalled ahead of Kevin Warsh’s first policy meeting as chair in June 2026, amid questions about his independence. The linked reports do not establish the statement’s exact date.

USA.title: Warren challenges Warsh to prove Fed independence
USA.summary: In an FT interview published ahead of Kevin Warsh’s first Federal Reserve meeting as chair, US Senator Elizabeth Warren said he must prove his independence. She alleged that he abandoned his longstanding inflation-hawk stance after President Trump demanded a chair who supported lower interest rates, and criticized his inability at his Senate hearing to identify an economic statement by Trump with which he disagreed. Warren did not advocate a specific interest-rate decision.

USA.title: Trump appoints Warsh with mandate to cut rates
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump reportedly installed Kevin Warsh as Federal Reserve chair with instructions to cut interest rates, making rate cuts a criterion for his selection. The linked reports do not establish the date of that intervention. At Warsh’s first policy meeting on June 17, 2026, the Fed instead kept rates at 3.5–3.75%, while Warsh emphasized restoring price stability. Trump reportedly brushed aside the unchanged-rate decision.

USA.title: Trump defers to Warsh after Fed holds rates
USA.summary: Asked by reporters in France during the G7 gathering about the Federal Reserve's decision to leave rates unchanged, US President Donald Trump said it was fine and did not matter. He praised Fed Chair Kevin Warsh and said he would follow what Warsh wanted. Despite Trump's previously reported preference for lower rates, this response contained no policy demand, criticism or threat.

USA.title: Wilson proposes a $250 banknote honoring Trump
USA.summary: Representative Joe Wilson of South Carolina advocated a new $250 U.S. banknote to commemorate 250 years of American independence, honor Donald Trump and compensate for the declining purchasing power of the $100 bill. The proposal concerns currency denomination rather than monetary easing or tightening; the report identifies no criticism of Federal Reserve officials or threat to their tenure or institutional autonomy.

USA.title: Trump shelves Fed digital currency plans
USA.summary: In a report contrasting US and European approaches to digital payments, US President Donald Trump was described as having shelved Federal Reserve plans for a digital currency in favor of privately issued stablecoins, predominantly linked to the dollar. The report did not specify when he took this action or describe any related threats or Federal Reserve response.

USA.title: Congress challenges Greenspan over regulatory failures
USA.summary: At a congressional hearing following the housing crash and financial crisis, lawmakers challenged former Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan over his regulatory judgment and reliance on financial institutions’ self-interest to protect shareholders. They questioned whether his ideology had been wrong and pressed him on his responsibility as a regulator. Greenspan acknowledged a flaw in his worldview and expressed shock that assumptions he had long considered supported by evidence had failed. The linked accounts do not establish the hearing’s exact date.

USA.title: Trump moves to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook
USA.summary: President Donald Trump moved to fire Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook in August 2025, citing alleged misrepresentations of her primary residence on mortgage paperwork and saying he had lost confidence in her integrity. Cook denied the allegations and had not been charged with a crime. Critics viewed the dismissal as a pretext to reshape the Fed amid Trump's frustration over interest rates. On June 29, 2026, the Supreme Court ruled 5–4 that Cook could remain in office while challenging her removal, emphasizing statutory protections and her opportunity to answer the allegations.

USA.title: Housing official accuses Cook of mortgage misrepresentation
USA.summary: Top housing official Bill Polte alleged in summer 2025 that Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook had misrepresented which of two homes was her primary residence on mortgage paperwork. The allegation supplied the stated basis for President Trump's subsequent attempt to dismiss her. The linked report says Cook had not been charged with a crime; it does not establish the exact date of Polte's accusation or attribute a policy demand or removal threat to him.

USA.title: Congress adds employment and price stability to Fed mandate
USA.summary: Congress changed the Federal Reserve’s statutory mandate in the late 1970s to include price stability and maximum employment. The story links the legislation to civil rights advocacy, including support from Coretta Scott King, who promoted full employment alongside broader social policies. It establishes no specific monetary policy demand or exact date for the legislative action.

USA.title: Velázquez challenges Warsh on independence from Trump
USA.summary: During Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh’s House Financial Services Committee appearance, Representative Nidia Velázquez questioned whether he worked for President Trump and how he would respond if the administration opposed Fed interest-rate decisions. Warsh defended the Fed’s congressionally established independence and said he would continue doing his job. Velázquez’s questioning did not establish a preferred interest-rate direction or an explicit threat.

USA.title: Trump says rate increases are not Warsh's decision alone
USA.summary: President Donald Trump said he met Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh weekly and respected him, but that raising interest rates was not a decision Warsh could make alone. The August 14, 2026 report recalled the remarks as occurring the previous week without identifying a specific day. No explicit rate demand, tenure threat or institutional change was reported in this intervention.

USA.title: Trump calls for lower interest rates in television appearance
USA.summary: In a television appearance reported as occurring that morning, Donald Trump called for lower US interest rates, saying, “We've got a strong economy and then of course we need to have a lower interest rate.” His remarks advocated monetary easing by the Federal Reserve without an accompanying threat or criticism of its competence.

USA.title: Vance urges Fed rate cuts at White House briefing
USA.summary: U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance urged the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates during a White House press briefing on September 3, 2026. At the same briefing, he answered questions about the conflict with Iran and its effects on energy markets. The report attributes no criticism of the Fed or threats to its officials or autonomy to Vance.

USA.title: Trump calls for lower rates when nominating Warsh
USA.summary: When nominating Kevin Warsh to chair the Federal Reserve, President Donald Trump made clear that he expected Warsh to lower short-term interest rates. The linked report does not date the nomination statement or describe any accompanying threat. It reports that investors subsequently questioned whether Warsh would accommodate Trump's preference for lower rates.

USA.title: Trump renews demand for world's lowest interest rates
USA.summary: In remarks replayed by FD Dagkoers on September 5, 2026 and described as made that week, US President Donald Trump renewed pressure on the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates below those of every other country. He called discussion of raising rates after strong economic data ridiculous, arguing that inflation fears unnecessarily constrain growth and suggesting that the economy could grow by as much as 20 percent. The precise date of his remarks was not established.

USA.title: Charges brought against former Fed chair
USA.summary: An NZZ Akzent episode reported that charges had been brought against an unnamed former Federal Reserve chair, citing the prosecution as a source of anxiety about the Fed's independence. It did not identify the prosecuting authority, specify the charges or establish any policy demand, removal threat or institutional change. The episode also stated that the Fed remained independent.

USA.title: Trump calls for a 0.5 percent interest rate
USA.summary: Donald Trump called for US interest rates to be 0.5 percent. A September 11 Bloomberg HT broadcast recalled his demand, noting that it would make raising rates harder for the new Federal Reserve chair amid oil-driven inflation concerns. The report did not specify when Trump made the statement or describe any accompanying threat.

USA.title: Trump calls for the world's lowest US interest rate
USA.summary: President Donald Trump said the United States should have the world's lowest interest rate, advocating easier Federal Reserve policy. A September 14 report recalled his demand ahead of the Fed meeting, contrasting presidential pressure for lower rates with market pressure for an increase.

USA.title: Trump says Fed chair will lower rates because of US economic strength
USA.summary: Donald Trump pressured Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh to lower interest rates, declaring that he would do so because the United States had the world's most efficient economy and excelled in artificial intelligence. The report discussed the remarks ahead of a Fed rate decision amid rising prices. No specific threat against Warsh or the Fed's autonomy was reported in this intervention.

USA.title: Vance appeals to Fed to cut rates
USA.summary: J.D. Vance publicly appealed to the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates, according to a September 14, 2026 report that described him as essentially pleading for a cut the previous week. The report provides no exact date for his appeal and attributes no criticism or threats to this intervention.

USA.title: Trump calls for world's lowest US interest rates from Ireland
USA.summary: Speaking from Ireland on Sunday, September 13, President Donald Trump reiterated that the United States should have the world's lowest interest rates, pressing the Federal Reserve under chair Kevin Warsh toward lower borrowing costs. His demand came ahead of the Fed's upcoming decision, amid elevated inflation and market expectations of a rate increase.

USA.title: Hassett warns Fed against election-period rate hike
USA.summary: Ahead of the Federal Reserve’s upcoming rate decision, National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett said President Trump would not be happy with a rate increase and argued that an independent Fed should stay out of the way of elections. His remarks urged the Fed against raising rates shortly before the November midterms, amid persistent inflation and market expectations of an increase.

USA.title: Trump brands Powell a numbskull over slow rate cuts
USA.summary: Donald Trump called then-Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell a “numbskull,” criticizing him for not cutting interest rates quickly enough. The linked story recalls this earlier intervention without establishing its date.

USA.title: Trump links rate-cut demand to threat to halt trade
USA.summary: Donald Trump demanded lower interest rates and said he would otherwise halt trade with all countries running trade surpluses with the United States. His remarks were recounted in a Norwegian-language discussion of rising US bond yields and Federal Reserve policy. The reported threat concerned trade, not Federal Reserve officials’ tenure or the bank’s institutional autonomy.

USA.title: Trump portrays Fed committee as forcing Warsh toward a rate hike
USA.summary: Ahead of the Federal Reserve’s rate decision, President Donald Trump suggested that Chair Kevin Warsh opposed raising interest rates but was being dragged toward a hike by a hostile committee. His portrayal blamed other Fed policymakers for prospective tightening, as markets widely expected an increase amid persistent inflation linked to the Iran war’s effect on oil prices.

USA.title: White House calls Fed rate increase unfortunate
USA.summary: An unnamed White House spokesman called the Federal Reserve’s quarter-percentage-point interest rate increase on September 16, 2026, “unfortunate,” expressing opposition to the tightening. The increase, the first since 2023, was approved unanimously. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh cited a strong labor market and inflation remaining above the bank’s 2% target. The spokesman made no reported threat or demand for institutional change.

USA.title: Trump calls prevailing interest rates ridiculous
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump described prevailing Federal Reserve interest rates as “ridiculous” amid his months-long demands for lower rates. The report contrasted his criticism with the Fed’s subsequent unanimous quarter-point rate increase to 3.75–4%, under Trump-appointed chair Kevin Walsh, aimed at containing inflation linked to rising energy prices. The report did not specify when Trump made the remark.

USA.title: Trump demands rapid rate cuts after Fed hike
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump demanded rapid interest-rate cuts in a capital-letter Truth Social post after the Federal Reserve unanimously raised rates by a quarter point to 3.75–4%. He argued that strong investment and US creditworthiness justified lower rates. Most linked accounts, including a quotation of the post, give his preferred rate as 1% or less; one describes it as one percentage point lower. The Fed cited persistently elevated inflation in explaining its increase.

USA.title: Trump threatens trade suspensions over Fed rate increases
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump recently threatened to suspend trade with individual countries if the Federal Reserve raised interest rates, seeking to prevent an increase. The report did not specify when he made the threat or explain the connection between trade suspensions and Fed policy. The Fed subsequently raised rates unanimously; this threat was separate from Trump's later Truth Social response.

USA.title: Trump accuses Fed governors of politically motivated rate hike
USA.summary: Following the Federal Reserve’s unanimous quarter-point rate increase to 3.75–4%, President Donald Trump accused its Board of Governors of acting politically to harm him. In social-media remarks and subsequent comments to reporters, he called the board hostile and reiterated that rates should quickly fall to 1% or lower. He spared Chair Kevin Warsh personal criticism, saying he had told him to vote with the board. The Fed justified the increase as necessary to bring persistent inflation toward its 2% target.

USA.title: Trump says US should have one percent interest rates
USA.summary: Responding to the Federal Reserve’s unanimous quarter-point rate increase, President Donald Trump demanded interest rates of 1% or less and rapid cuts. He called the Fed board hostile and political and said it was doing the wrong thing. Trump told reporters that he had spoken with chair Kevin Warsh before the decision and had told him to vote with the board, while expressing continued confidence in him. He did not threaten dismissal. Warsh declined to discuss presidential conversations and reiterated the Fed’s independence.

USA.title: Trump demands world's lowest interest rate before Fed meeting
USA.summary: Days before the Federal Reserve's September 2026 meeting, President Donald Trump demanded that the United States pay the world's lowest interest rate, arguing that its economic strength and creditworthiness justified this regardless of policy formulas. He asserted that he knew more about formulas than anyone. His remarks pressed for lower rates as rising inflation strengthened the case for a rate increase; the story does not establish the exact date of the statement.

USA.title: Trump says he wants a Fed chair who will cut rates
USA.summary: Donald Trump said he wanted a Federal Reserve chair who would cut interest rates. A September 27, 2026 podcast recalled the undated statement, explaining that it initially contributed to market doubts about whether Kevin Warsh would raise rates to combat inflation. The intervention expressed a preference for easing without an explicit threat or institutional demand.

USA.title: Trump renews attacks on Powell after watchdog clearance
USA.summary: US President Donald Trump renewed attacks on former Federal Reserve chair Jerome Powell after the Fed's inspector general cleared Powell of accusations. Linked reporting also described presidential pressure for Powell to resign. Trump regarded current Fed monetary policy as too restrictive and favored lower interest rates.
